scope: New York State law applying statewide (including in NYC), plus federal overlays that change the NY landlord's or manager's decision. The NYC-only layer is external (NYC:*). Stage A legal meaning only: no clocks, formulas or data bindings. Prepared 2026-09-28; second pass 2026-09-28 (see SECOND_PASS_NY.md); resolution pass 2026-09-28 (see RESOLUTION_NY.md; zero open questions); aperture: units in New York City and the state law that governs them (Owen, 2026-09-28); pending Owen's acceptance.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: Money is deposited or advanced on a contract or license agreement for the use or rental of real property, as security for performance or to be applied to payments when due. Applies to every such deposit in NY regardless of unit type or regulatory status, including rent-stabilized, rent-controlled and small-building units.
atoms.effect: Section 7-103 governs that money (trust, bank notice, interest). Nothing in the section limits it to dwellings or to buildings of a given size; only subdivision 2-a is size-limited.
atoms.quote: Whenever money shall be deposited or advanced on a contract or license agreement for the use or rental of real property as security for performance of the contract or agreement or to be applied to payments upon such contract or agreement when due

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A deposit or advance within 7-103(1) is held, until repaid or applied.
atoms.effect: The deposit, with any interest accruing on it, stays the tenant's money; the landlord holds it in trust, may not mingle it with personal money, and it is not the landlord's asset. It may be disposed of only as 7-105 provides on a transfer. Commingling forfeits the landlord's right to use the deposit at all (NY:CASE-Paterno-commingling-forfeiture).
atoms.quote: such money, with interest accruing thereon, if any, until repaid or so applied, shall continue to be the money of the person making such deposit or advance and shall be held in trust by the person with whom such deposit or advance shall be made and shall not be mingled with the personal moneys or become an asset of the person receiving the same, but may be disposed of as provided in section 7-105 of this chapter

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: The landlord deposits the security money in a banking organization.
atoms.effect: The landlord must then notify each depositor in writing of the bank's name and address and the amount deposited; the bank must have a place of business in NY.
atoms.quote: Whenever the person receiving money so deposited or advanced shall deposit such money in a banking organization, such person shall thereupon notify in writing each of the persons making such security deposit or advance, giving the name and address of the banking organization in which the deposit of security money is made, and the amount of such deposit. Deposits in a banking organization pursuant to the provisions of this subdivision shall be made in a banking organization having a place of business within the state.
atoms.cross_time: Duty arises at deposit (move-in or later); a missing bank notice is a pre-existing compliance fact the settlement inherits.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: The landlord holds the security money in an interest-bearing account.
atoms.effect: The landlord may keep, as administration expenses, a sum equal to 1% a year on the security money; this is in lieu of all other administrative and custodial expenses (no other admin/custody charge against the deposit).
atoms.quote: If the person depositing such security money in a banking organization shall deposit same in an interest bearing account, he shall be entitled to receive, as administration expenses, a sum equivalent to one per cent per annum upon the security money so deposited, which shall be in lieu of all other administrative and custodial expenses.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: Interest is paid by the bank on the security money.
atoms.effect: The interest balance after the 1% fee is the tenant's money. It is either held in trust until repaid or applied to rent, or paid to the tenant annually. At settlement, any interest balance not already paid or applied is owed to the tenant with the deposit.
atoms.quote: The balance of the interest paid by the banking organization shall be the money of the person making the deposit or advance and shall either be held in trust by the person with whom such deposit or advance shall be made, until repaid or applied for the use or rental of the leased premises, or annually paid to the person making the deposit of security money.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: The deposit or advance is for the rental of property containing six or more family dwelling units.
atoms.effect: The landlord must hold the deposit in an interest-bearing account at a NY banking organization earning the prevailing area rate. Units are counted per building (NY:ADJ-7103-2a-building-count). Below six units in the building, this subdivision does not require an interest-bearing account.
judgment_terms: prevailing rate earned by other such deposits in the area
atoms.quote: Whenever the money so deposited or advanced is for the rental of property containing six or more family dwelling units, the person receiving such money shall, subject to the provisions of this section, deposit it in an interest bearing account in a banking organization within the state which account shall earn interest at a rate which shall be the prevailing rate earned by other such deposits made with banking organizations in such area.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: The lease terminates at a time other than when the bank regularly pays interest.
atoms.effect: The landlord must pay the tenant the interest it is able to collect as of the lease termination date.
judgment_terms: interest the landlord 'is able to collect' at termination
atoms.quote: In the event that a lease terminates other than at the time that a banking organization in such area regularly pays interest, the person depositing such security money shall pay over to his tenant such interest as he is able to collect at the date of such lease termination.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A lease or agreement term by which the depositor waives any provision of 7-103.
atoms.effect: The waiver is absolutely void.
atoms.quote: Any provision of such a contract or agreement whereby a person who so deposits or advances money waives any provision of this section is absolutely void.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.actor: transferring owner or lessee (and its agents)
atoms.condition: The holder of a tenant's deposit conveys the property or assigns its lease, or a foreclosure receiver qualifies, or a referee conveys in foreclosure with no receiver.
atoms.effect: At delivery of the deed/assignment or within 5 days after (or within 5 days after the receiver qualifies), the holder must turn the deposit over to the grantee, assignee, receiver or foreclosure purchaser, and notify the tenant by registered or certified mail of the turnover and the transferee's name and address.
atoms.quote: at the time of the delivery of the deed or instrument or assignment or within five days thereafter, or within five days after the receiver shall have qualified, deal with the security deposit as follows: Turn over to his or its grantee or assignee, or to the receiver in the foreclosure action, or to the purchaser at the foreclosure sale if a receiver shall not have been appointed and qualified the sum so deposited, and notify the tenant or licensee by registered or certified mail of such turning over and the name and address of such grantee, assignee, purchaser or receiver.
atoms.cross_time: Transfer mid-tenancy fixes who owes the refund at move-out.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: The owner or lessee turns the deposit over to the grantee, assignee, foreclosure purchaser or receiver.
atoms.effect: The transferor is relieved of liability to the tenant for repayment; the transferee becomes responsible for returning it, unless it in turn transfers it under 7-105(1) with notice before the lease term expires. A receiver holds it subject to the foreclosure court's order.
atoms.quote: is hereby relieved of and from liability to the tenant or licensee for the repayment thereof; and the transferee of such security deposit is hereby made responsible for the return thereof to the tenant or licensee

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: The landlord-tenant agreement is inconsistent with 7-105.
atoms.effect: Section 7-105 does not apply.
judgment_terms: whether a lease term is 'inconsistent' with 7-105
atoms.quote: The provisions of this section shall not apply if the agreement between the landlord and tenant or licensee is inconsistent herewith.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: Failure to comply with 7-105.
atoms.effect: Misdemeanor.
atoms.quote: Any failure to comply with this section is a misdemeanor.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 1984 (L.1984 c.917); current wording from L.2025 c.436
atoms.condition: The dwelling unit is subject to the NYC Rent Stabilization Law of 1969 or the Emergency Tenant Protection Act of 1974 (inside or outside NYC).
atoms.effect: Section 7-107 applies to the unit, and only to such units. Because 7-108(1) excludes any unit 'specifically referred to in 7-107', such a unit is outside 7-108 entirely, whatever its lease date. Which 7-107 text applies turns on the date the operative lease or renewal was entered into: on or after 2025-11-15, amended 7-107; before it, former 7-107 (successor liability only: NY:GOL-7-107-pre2025(1)-scope).
atoms.quote: This section shall apply only to dwelling units subject to the New York city rent stabilization law of nineteen hundred sixty-nine or the emergency tenant protection act of nineteen seventy-four.

atoms.condition: A rent-stabilized or ETPA unit (7-107(1)).
atoms.effect: Amended 7-107 (subdivisions 2-10: cap, refund, inspections, 14-day statement, forfeiture, burden, damages, successor liability, waiver) applies only to a lease, rental agreement or renewal entered into on or after the 30th day after the act became law (signed 2025-10-16, so 2025-11-15). The test is the date the lease or renewal was entered into, not the date its term starts. For a stabilized/ETPA lease or renewal entered into before that date, former 7-107 continues (NY:GOL-7-107-pre2025(1)-scope): no statutory cap, deadline, statement or forfeiture. c.436 was signed without an approval memo (no agreed chapter amendment), and the section text at nysenate.gov on 2026-09-28 matches the enacted bill.
atoms.quote: This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have become a law and shall apply to any lease or rental agreement or renewal of a lease or rental agreement entered into on or after such date.
atoms.cross_time: Routes by the date the operative lease or renewal was entered, not by the move-out date. Signing date from Assembly actions: '10/16/2025SIGNED CHAP.436'.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA unit; lease or renewal entered on or after 2025-11-15.
atoms.effect: No deposit or advance may exceed one month's rent. Any excess held is not lawfully held and is refundable.
atoms.quote: No deposit or advance shall exceed the amount of one month's rent, under any contract for the lease or tenancy of a dwelling unit subject to this section.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA unit under amended 7-107; tenant vacates.
atoms.effect: The whole deposit or advance is refundable except amounts lawfully retained for the reasonable and itemized costs of: non-payment of rent; damage caused by the tenant beyond normal wear and tear; non-payment of utility charges payable directly to the landlord under the lease; moving and storage of the tenant's belongings. These are the only retention categories; fees are excluded (NY:ADJ-no-fee-retention).
judgment_terms: damage beyond normal wear and tear
utility charges payable directly to the landlord under the lease
atoms.quote: The entire amount of the deposit or advance, shall be refundable to the tenant upon the tenant's vacating of the premises except for an amount lawfully retained for the reasonable and itemized costs due to non-payment of rent, damage caused by the tenant beyond normal wear and tear, non-payment of utility charges payable directly to the landlord under the terms of the lease or tenancy, and moving and storage of the tenant's belongings.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA unit under amended 7-107.
atoms.effect: No amount may be retained for ordinary wear and tear of occupancy or for damage caused by a prior tenant.
judgment_terms: ordinary wear and tear of occupancy
damage caused by a prior tenant
atoms.quote: The landlord may not retain any amount of the deposit for costs relating to ordinary wear and tear of occupancy or damage caused by a prior tenant.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA unit under amended 7-107; after initial lease signing, before occupancy.
atoms.effect: Landlord must offer the tenant a joint inspection. If the tenant requests it, the parties must sign, before occupancy, a written agreement on the unit's condition noting existing defects or damage.
atoms.quote: After initial lease signing but before the tenant begins occupancy, the landlord shall offer the tenant the opportunity to inspect the premises with the landlord or the landlord's agent to determine the condition of the property. If the tenant requests such inspection, the parties shall execute a written agreement before the tenant begins occupancy of the unit attesting to the condition of the property and specifically noting any existing defects or damages.
atoms.cross_time: Move-in duty; its record constrains move-out deductions. Applies only where the initial lease signing falls under amended 7-107 (on/after 2025-11-15); a renewal-only tenancy has no 'initial lease signing' under the amended text.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: A move-in condition agreement exists under 7-107(4); tenant vacates.
atoms.effect: No deduction for any condition, defect or damage noted in the agreement. The agreement is admissible on move-in condition only in deposit return/amount proceedings.
judgment_terms: whether a claimed item is a condition 'noted in such agreement'
atoms.quote: Upon the tenant's vacating of the premises, the landlord may not retain any amount of the deposit or advance due to any condition, defect, or damage noted in such agreement. The agreement shall be admissible as evidence of the condition of the premises at the beginning of occupancy only in proceedings related to the return or amount of the security deposit.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA unit under amended 7-107; either party has notified intention to terminate; the tenant did not terminate on less than two weeks' notice.
atoms.effect: Within a reasonable time after that notification, landlord must tell the tenant in writing of the right to request a pre-vacate inspection and to be present.
judgment_terms: what counts as notification of intention to terminate
atoms.quote: Within a reasonable time after notification of either party's intention to terminate the tenancy, unless the tenant terminates the tenancy with less than two weeks' notice, the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant's right to request an inspection before vacating the premises and of the tenant's right to be present at the inspection.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Tenant requests the pre-vacate inspection.
atoms.effect: Inspection no earlier than two weeks and no later than one week before the end of the tenancy, on at least 48 hours' written notice of date and time. Afterwards landlord must give an itemized statement of repairs or cleaning proposed as deduction bases; tenant may cure before the tenancy ends. The statement is admissible only in deposit proceedings.
atoms.quote: If the tenant requests such an inspection, the inspection shall be made no earlier than two weeks and no later than one week before the end of the tenancy. The landlord shall provide at least forty-eight hours written notice of the date and time of the inspection. After the inspection, the landlord shall provide the tenant with an itemized statement specifying repairs or cleaning that are proposed to be the basis of any deductions from the tenant's deposit. The tenant shall have the opportunity to cure any such condition before the end of the tenancy.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA unit under amended 7-107; tenant has vacated.
atoms.effect: Within 14 days after vacating, landlord must provide an itemized statement of the basis for any amount retained and return the remainder to the tenant.
atoms.quote: Within fourteen days after the tenant has vacated the premises, the landlord shall provide the tenant with an itemized statement indicating the basis for the amount of the deposit retained, if any, and shall return any remaining portion of the deposit to the tenant.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Landlord fails to provide the statement and the deposit within 14 days.
atoms.effect: Landlord forfeits any right to retain any portion of the deposit. No intent element.
atoms.quote: If a landlord fails to provide the tenant with the statement and deposit within fourteen days, the landlord shall forfeit any right to retain any portion of the deposit.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: An action or proceeding disputes the amount retained.
atoms.effect: Landlord bears the burden of proving the reasonableness of the amount retained.
atoms.quote: In any action or proceeding disputing the amount of any portion of the deposit retained, the landlord shall bear the burden of proof as to the reasonableness of the amount retained.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: A person violates amended 7-107.
atoms.effect: Liable for actual damages; if found to have violated willfully, punitive damages up to twice the deposit or advance.
atoms.quote: Any person who violates the provisions of this section shall be liable for actual damages, provided a person found to have willfully violated this section shall be liable for punitive damages of up to twice the amount of the deposit or advance.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.actor: grantee or assignee of the premises
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA premises conveyed; the deposit was not turned over under 7-105; grantee has actual knowledge of the deposit.
atoms.effect: Grantee/assignee is also liable to the tenant for repayment of the deposit plus accrued interest.
atoms.quote: In circumstances where any sum of money or any other thing of value deposited as security for the full performance by a tenant of the terms of their lease is not turned over to a successor in interest pursuant to section 7-105 of this title, the grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall also be liable to such tenant, upon conveyance of such leased premises, for the repayment of any such security deposit, plus accrued interest, as to which such grantee or assignee has actual knowledge.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Determining the grantee's actual knowledge.
atoms.effect: Deemed actual knowledge of any deposit (i) placed in a bank under 7-103(2-a) in the 6 months before closing, (ii) acknowledged in a lease in effect at closing, or (iii) supported by the tenant's documentary evidence under (c).
atoms.quote: a grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall be deemed to have actual knowledge of any security deposit which is (i) deposited at any time during the six months immediately prior to closing or other transfer of title in any banking organization pursuant to subdivision two-a of section 7-103 of this title, or (ii) acknowledged in any lease in effect at the time of closing or other transfer of title, or (iii) supported by documentary evidence provided by the tenant or lessee as set forth in paragraph (c) of this subdivision.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: No record of the deposit under (b)(i) or (ii) after a transfer.
atoms.effect: Grantee must notify the tenant in writing within 30 days after closing that there is no record and that the tenant has no further recourse against the grantee unless it supplies documentary evidence (cancelled check, receipt, or lease signed by a predecessor) within 30 days of receiving the notice. If the grantee does not send the notice, the tenant may produce the evidence at any time.
atoms.quote: the grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall be obligated to notify the tenant thereof in writing no later than thirty days following the closing or other transfer of title to the fact that there is no record of a security deposit for said leased premises and that unless the tenant within thirty days after receiving notice provides them or it with documentary evidence of deposit, the tenant shall have no further recourse against them or it for said security deposit.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: No record of a deposit for the premises at transfer.
atoms.effect: Grantee may demand the grantor fund an escrow equal to one month's rent to hold it harmless against a later tenant claim.
atoms.quote: The grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall have the right to demand that the grantor or assignor thereof establish an escrow account equal to one month's rent for any leased premises for which there is no record of a security deposit pursuant to paragraph (b) of this subdivision

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: A receiver's liability for a deposit plus interest.
atoms.effect: Limited to the deposit actually turned over to it under 7-105(1) plus operating income in excess of expenses during the receivership.
atoms.quote: The liability of a receiver for payment of any security deposit plus accrued interest pursuant to this subdivision shall be limited to the amount of such deposit actually turned over to them or it pursuant to subdivision one of section 7-105 of this title and to the operating income in excess of expenses generated during their or its period of receivership.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2025-11-15 (30th day after L.2025 c.436 was signed on 2025-10-16; s.2); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: A tenant agreement waiving or modifying 7-107 rights.
atoms.effect: Absolutely void.
atoms.quote: Any agreement by a lessee or tenant of a dwelling waiving or modifying their rights as set forth in this section shall be absolutely void.

atoms.instrument: GOL 7-107 as in force before L.2025 c.436 (text read from the bracketed deletions in the enacted bill)
atoms.effective_to: 2025-11-15 for leases/renewals entered on or after that date; continues for stabilized/ETPA leases and renewals entered before it, because L.2025 c.436 s.2 limits the amended text to later leases
atoms.actor: grantee or assignee of a stabilized/ETPA unit
atoms.condition: Stabilized/ETPA unit conveyed; operative lease/renewal entered before 2025-11-15; the predecessor was liable for the deposit.
atoms.effect: The grantee/assignee is liable to the tenant for the deposit plus accrued interest whether or not it received the deposit at conveyance (no actual-knowledge limit).
atoms.quote: [(a)  Any  grantee or assignee of any dwelling unit referred to in subdivision one of this section shall be liable to a tenant for any  sum of  money or any other thing of value deposited as security for the full performance by such tenant of the terms of his lease, plus  any  accrued interest,  if  his  or  its  predecessor in interest was liable for such funds. Such liability shall attach  whether  or  not  the  successor  in interest  has,  upon  the conveyance of such dwelling unit, received the sum as deposited.
atoms.cross_time: The former text governs stabilized/ETPA leases and renewals entered before 2025-11-15: L.2025 c.436 s.2 applies the amended 7-107 only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered on or after that date.

atoms.instrument: GOL 7-107 as in force before L.2025 c.436
atoms.effective_to: 2025-11-15 for leases/renewals entered on or after that date; continues for stabilized/ETPA leases and renewals entered before it, because L.2025 c.436 s.2 limits the amended text to later leases
atoms.condition: Receiver of a stabilized/ETPA building; pre-2025-11-15 lease.
atoms.effect: Receiver's liability limited to the deposit actually turned over plus operating income over expenses during receivership.
atoms.quote: (b) The liability of a receiver for payment of  any  security  deposit plus  accrued  interest pursuant to this subdivision shall be limited to the amount of such deposit actually turned over to him or it pursuant to subdivision one of section 7-105 of this chapter

atoms.instrument: GOL 7-107 as in force before L.2025 c.436
atoms.effective_to: 2025-11-15 for leases/renewals entered on or after that date; continues for stabilized/ETPA leases and renewals entered before it, because L.2025 c.436 s.2 limits the amended text to later leases
atoms.condition: Waiver of former 7-107 rights; pre-2025-11-15 lease.
atoms.effect: Void.
atoms.quote: 3. [Any agreement by a lessee or tenant of a dwelling unit waiving  or modifying  his  rights  as  set  forth in this section shall be void]

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14 (current wording)
atoms.condition: Any dwelling unit in residential premises in NY.
atoms.effect: Section 7-108 applies unless the unit is specifically referred to in 7-107 (rent-stabilized or ETPA units, whatever their lease date). No building-size or written-lease condition in the current text. The 2019 heading names 7-108 'Deposits made by tenants of non-rent stabilized dwelling units', and the 2025 sponsors confirm the exclusion (NY:L2025-c436-memo-gap). For leases entered before 2019-07-14 and not renewed, the old scope applies (NY:GOL-7-108(1)-pre2019).
atoms.quote: This section shall apply to all dwelling units in residential premises, unless such dwelling unit is specifically referred to in section 7-107 of this title.
atoms.cross_time: Pre-HSTPA 7-108(1) was limited to units with written leases in premises of six or more units and to rent-controlled units, and 7-108 then held only successor-liability rules (L.2019 c.36 Part M s.25 bracketed text). That scope governs leases entered before 2019-07-14 and not renewed (NY:GOL-7-108(1)-pre2019).

atoms.instrument: L.2019 c.36 (HSTPA) Part M

Seasonal exception added 2021-09-20 (L.2021 c.428); co-op exception added 2021-12-22 (L.2021 c.789); current wording from L.2022 c.93
atoms.condition: Unit under 7-108(1-a); lease/renewal on or after 2019-07-14.
atoms.effect: No deposit or advance may exceed one month's rent, unless it is for a qualifying seasonal use dwelling unit (subs. 4-5) or an owner-occupied cooperative apartment (sub. 6). An 'advance' is rent paid ahead for a later period, such as last month's rent; deposit and advance together are capped at one month. The first month's rent paid at signing for the first rental period is rent, not an advance. Any excess is refundable at settlement.
atoms.quote: No deposit or advance shall exceed the amount of one month's rent, unless the deposit or advance is for a seasonal use dwelling unit as provided for in subdivisions four and five of this section, or unless the deposit or advance is for an owner-occupied cooperative apartment as provided for in subdivision six of this section.
atoms.cross_time: Cap is set at move-in; an over-cap amount held at move-out is not lawfully held.

construction.quote: The one-month limit means that a landlord cannot ask for last month’s rent and a security deposit.

atoms.reasoning: An advance is money paid before it is due. Rent for the first period, paid at signing, is due then and is not paid ahead. The Attorney General, who enforces the article (GOL 7-109), reads the cap as reaching last month's rent together with a deposit.

atoms.condition: Unit under 7-108(1-a); tenant vacates.
atoms.effect: The whole deposit or advance is refundable except amounts lawfully retained for the reasonable and itemized costs of: non-payment of rent; damage caused by the tenant beyond normal wear and tear; non-payment of utility charges payable directly to the landlord under the lease; moving and storage of the tenant's belongings. Only these categories may be retained. Fees and other charges are not retained (NY:ADJ-no-fee-retention); lawful ones are pursued separately.
judgment_terms: damage beyond normal wear and tear
utility charges payable directly to the landlord under the lease
atoms.quote: The entire amount of the deposit or advance shall be refundable to the tenant upon the tenant's vacating of the premises except for an amount lawfully retained for the reasonable and itemized costs due to non-payment of rent, damage caused by the tenant beyond normal wear and tear, non-payment of utility charges payable directly to the landlord under the terms of the lease or tenancy, and moving and storage of the tenant's belongings.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Unit under 7-108(1-a).
atoms.effect: No retention for ordinary wear and tear of occupancy or for damage caused by a prior tenant.
judgment_terms: ordinary wear and tear of occupancy
damage caused by a prior tenant
atoms.quote: The landlord may not retain any amount of the deposit for costs relating to ordinary wear and tear of occupancy or damage caused by a prior tenant.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Unit under 7-108(1-a); after initial lease signing, before occupancy.
atoms.effect: Landlord must offer a joint move-in inspection; if the tenant requests it, the parties must sign before occupancy a written condition agreement noting existing defects or damage.
atoms.quote: After initial lease signing but before the tenant begins occupancy, the landlord shall offer the tenant the opportunity to inspect the premises with the landlord or the landlord's agent to determine the condition of the property. If the tenant requests such inspection, the parties shall execute a written agreement before the tenant begins occupancy of the unit attesting to the condition of the property and specifically noting any existing defects or damages.
atoms.cross_time: Move-in duty whose record constrains move-out deductions. Toporek holds that by the statute's plain terms only (e) carries forfeiture, so breach of (c) carries no forfeiture; 7-108(1-a)(g) actual damages apply on its text.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: A move-in condition agreement exists; tenant vacates.
atoms.effect: No deduction for any condition, defect or damage noted in it; the agreement is admissible on move-in condition only in deposit return/amount proceedings.
judgment_terms: whether a claimed item is a condition 'noted in such agreement'
atoms.quote: Upon the tenant's vacating of the premises, the landlord may not retain any amount of the deposit or advance due to any condition, defect, or damage noted in such agreement. The agreement shall be admissible as evidence of the condition of the premises at the beginning of occupancy only in proceedings related to the return or amount of the security deposit.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Unit under 7-108(1-a); either party has notified intention to terminate; tenant did not terminate on less than two weeks' notice.
atoms.effect: Within a reasonable time after that notification, landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the right to request a pre-vacate inspection and to be present. Breach does not trigger forfeiture (NY:CASE-Toporek-forfeiture-scope).
judgment_terms: what counts as notification of intention to terminate
atoms.quote: Within a reasonable time after notification of either party's intention to terminate the tenancy, unless the tenant terminates the tenancy with less than two weeks' notice, the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant's right to request an inspection before vacating the premises and of the tenant's right to be present at the inspection.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Tenant requests the pre-vacate inspection.
atoms.effect: Inspection between two weeks and one week before the end of the tenancy, on at least 48 hours' written notice; afterwards an itemized statement of repairs or cleaning proposed as deduction bases; tenant may cure before the tenancy ends; statement admissible only in deposit proceedings. 48 hours is an hours period, not a day period (GCN 20 two-day rule not engaged on its words).
atoms.quote: If the tenant requests such an inspection, the inspection shall be made no earlier than two weeks and no later than one week before the end of the tenancy. The landlord shall provide at least forty-eight hours written notice of the date and time of the inspection. After the inspection, the landlord shall provide the tenant with an itemized statement specifying repairs or cleaning that are proposed to be the basis of any deductions from the tenant's deposit. The tenant shall have the opportunity to cure any such condition before the end of the tenancy.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Unit under 7-108(1-a); tenant has vacated.
atoms.effect: Within 14 days after vacating, landlord must provide an itemized statement of the basis for any amount retained (including retention for unpaid rent: Mihalow) and return the remainder of the deposit to the tenant. Where the building has 6+ units or the deposit is in an interest-bearing account, the remainder includes the tenant's interest balance (7-103(2), (2-b)).
atoms.quote: Within fourteen days after the tenant has vacated the premises, the landlord shall provide the tenant with an itemized statement indicating the basis for the amount of the deposit retained, if any, and shall return any remaining portion of the deposit to the tenant.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: Landlord fails to provide the statement and the deposit within 14 days.
atoms.effect: The landlord forfeits any right to retain any portion of the deposit; there is no intent element. Only the right to retain the deposit is forfeited. The landlord's claims for rent, damage and other lawful charges survive and are pursued separately or by counterclaim on proof (NY:ADJ-forfeiture-claims-survive).
atoms.quote: If a landlord fails to provide the tenant with the statement and deposit within fourteen days, the landlord shall forfeit any right to retain any portion of the deposit.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: An action or proceeding disputes the amount retained.
atoms.effect: Landlord bears the burden of proving the reasonableness of the amount retained.
atoms.quote: In any action or proceeding disputing the amount of any amount of the deposit retained, the landlord shall bear the burden of proof as to the reasonableness of the amount retained.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.effective_from: 2019-07-14 (30th day after L.2019 c.36 became law on 2019-06-14; Part M s.29); applies only to leases, rental agreements and renewals entered into on or after that date
atoms.condition: A person violates 7-108(1-a).
atoms.effect: Liable for actual damages (Appellate Term: the retained deposit). A person found to have violated willfully is liable for punitive damages of up to twice the deposit or advance. The meaning of 'willfully' is stated in NY:ADJ-willful-standard.
atoms.quote: Any person who violates the provisions of this subdivision shall be liable for actual damages, provided a person found to have willfully violated this subdivision shall be liable for punitive damages of up to twice the amount of the deposit or advance.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.actor: grantee or assignee of the premises
atoms.condition: Premises under 7-108 (including rent-controlled units) conveyed; the deposit was not turned over under 7-105; grantee has actual knowledge of the deposit.
atoms.effect: Grantee/assignee is also liable to the tenant for repayment of the deposit plus accrued interest.
atoms.quote: In circumstances where any sum of money or any other thing of value deposited as security for the full performance by a tenant of the terms of his lease is not turned over to a successor in interest pursuant to section 7-105 of this chapter, the grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall also be liable to such tenant, upon conveyance of such leased premises, for the repayment of any such security deposit, plus accrued interest, as to which such grantee or assignee has actual knowledge.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.condition: Determining the grantee's actual knowledge.
atoms.effect: Deemed knowledge of a deposit (i) banked under 7-103(2-a) within 6 months before closing, (ii) acknowledged in a lease in effect at closing, or (iii) supported by tenant documentary evidence under (c).
atoms.quote: a grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall be deemed to have actual knowledge of any security deposit which is (i) deposited at any time during the six months immediately prior to closing or other transfer of title in any banking organization pursuant to subdivision two-a of section 7-103 of this chapter, or (ii) acknowledged in any lease in effect at the time of closing or other transfer of title, or (iii) supported by documentary evidence provided by the tenant or lessee as set forth in paragraph (c) of this subdivision.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.condition: No record of a deposit under (b)(i)-(ii) after transfer.
atoms.effect: Grantee must notify the tenant in writing within 30 days after closing; the tenant then has 30 days from receipt to produce documentary evidence (cancelled check, receipt, or lease signed by a predecessor) or lose recourse against the grantee. If the grantee does not notify, the tenant may produce evidence at any time.
atoms.quote: the grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall be obligated to notify the tenant thereof in writing no later than thirty days following the closing or other transfer of title to the fact that there is no record of a security deposit for said leased premises and that unless the tenant within thirty days after receiving notice provides him or it with documentary evidence of deposit, the tenant shall have no further recourse against him or it for said security deposit.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.condition: No record of a deposit at transfer.
atoms.effect: Grantee may demand that the grantor fund an escrow of one month's rent to hold it harmless.
atoms.quote: The grantee or assignee of the leased premises shall have the right to demand that the grantor or assignor thereof establish an escrow account equal to one month's rent for any leased premises for which there is no record of a security deposit pursuant to paragraph (b) of this subdivision

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law art. 7 title 1
atoms.condition: Receiver liability for a deposit plus interest.
atoms.effect: Limited to the deposit actually turned over plus operating income over expenses during receivership.
atoms.quote: The liability of a receiver for payment of any security deposit plus accrued interest pursuant to this subdivision shall be limited to the amount of such deposit actually turned over to him or it pursuant to subdivision one of section 7-105 of this chapter and to the operating income in excess of expenses generated during his or its period of receivership.

atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: Construing any NY statute, including the GOL, RPL and GBL provisions in this file.
atoms.effect: The General Construction Law (including ss.19, 20, 24, 25-a, 30) applies unless the statute's object, context or other law shows a different meaning was intended.
judgment_terms: whether a statute's object or context indicates a different meaning
atoms.quote: This chapter is applicable to every statute unless its general object, or the context of the language construed, or other provisions of law indicate that a different meaning or application was intended from that required to be given by this chapter.

atoms.instrument: NY General Construction Law
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A statute counts days.
atoms.effect: A calendar day runs midnight to midnight.
atoms.quote: A calendar day includes the time from midnight to midnight.

atoms.instrument: NY General Construction Law
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A statute sets a number of days from a certain day or event (e.g., 14 days after the tenant vacated).
atoms.effect: Count calendar days, excluding the day of the event (the reckoning day). A two-day period excludes an intervening Saturday, Sunday or public holiday.
atoms.quote: A number of days specified as a period from a certain day within which or after or before which an act is authorized or required to be done means such number of calendar days exclusive of the calendar day from which the reckoning is made.

atoms.instrument: NY General Construction Law
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A period runs from a specified event.
atoms.effect: The event day is the reckoning day and is excluded.
atoms.quote: In computing any specified period of time from a specified event, the day upon which the event happens is deemed the day from which the reckoning is made. The day from which any specified period of time is reckoned shall be excluded in making the reckoning.

atoms.instrument: NY General Construction Law
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A statutory period computed from a certain day ends on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday (e.g., the 7-108(1-a)(e) 14th day).
atoms.effect: The act may be done on the next succeeding business day. Periods set by contract are governed by GCN 25 instead.
judgment_terms: business day (not defined in the section; read as a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday)
atoms.quote: When any period of time, computed from a certain day, within which or after which or before which an act is authorized or required to be done, ends on a Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday, such act may be done on the next succeeding business day
atoms.cross_time: Holiday calendar becomes a Stage D input.

atoms.instrument: NY General Construction Law
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: The period is specified by contract (e.g., lease rent due date, lease notice period).
atoms.effect: Extension governed by GCN 25, not 25-a.
atoms.quote: except that where a period of time specified by contract ends on a Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday, the extension of such period is governed by section twenty-five of this chapter.

atoms.instrument: NY General Construction Law
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A lease requires payment or performance on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, or within a period ending on one (e.g., rent due on the 1st falling on a Sunday).
atoms.effect: Unless the contract expressly or impliedly shows a different intent, payment or performance on the next business day has the same effect. Bears on whether rent is 'late' for 238-a(2).
judgment_terms: contract expressly or impliedly indicates a different intent
atoms.quote: unless the contract expressly or impliedly indicates a different intent, such payment may be made or condition performed on the next succeeding business day

atoms.quote: The term public holiday includes the following days in each year:

atoms.instrument: NY General Construction Law
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A statute or lease sets a number of months (e.g., 'one month before the expiration' in RPL 232-b).

atoms.quote: A number of months after or before a certain day shall be computed by counting such number of calendar months from such day, exclusive of the calendar month in which such day occurs

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 7
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A person occupies real property under an agreement not made by deed (e.g., holdover after the lease ends, occupancy without a lease).
atoms.effect: Landlord may recover reasonable compensation for use and occupation; a lease may be used as evidence of the amount.
judgment_terms: reasonable compensation for use and occupation
atoms.quote: The landlord may recover a reasonable compensation for the use and occupation of real property, by any person, under an agreement, not made by deed; and a parol lease or other agreement may be used as evidence of the amount to which he is entitled.

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 7
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: Leased property or the reversion is conveyed.
atoms.effect: The grantee has the grantor's remedies for rent and other lease charges falling due after title passes, and for waste or other breach. Rent and charges that fell due before title passed belong to the seller unless the seller assigned them to the buyer in writing; the buyer, holding the deposit under GOL 7-105, may not keep it for pre-sale arrears it does not own, so its statement itemizes only amounts owed to it. An assignee of pre-sale arrears sues on them as an assignee.
atoms.quote: The grantee of leased real property, or of a reversion thereof, or of any rent, the devisee or assignee of the lessor of such a lease, or the heir or personal representative of either of them, has the same remedies, by entry, action or otherwise, for the nonperformance of any agreement contained in the assigned lease for the recovery of rent, for the doing of any waste, or for other cause of forfeiture as his grantor or lessor had

construction.quote: There is no provision in the deed purporting to transfer the arrearage of rents to the grantee, and in the absence of such transfer the present landlord had no right to rents which had become due at the time of the passing of title.
the reference in section 223 of the Real Property Law to assignees of rents is to assignees of rents accruing after the grants therein referred to.

atoms.reasoning: Getty Realty (App Term 1st Dept 1939) holds that rent due when title passes stays with the grantor absent a transfer, and reads RPL 223's assignees of rents as assignees of rent accruing after the grant.

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 7
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: A residential tenant asks to assign the lease; the lease gives no greater right.
atoms.effect: Owner may withhold consent without cause, but if it unreasonably withholds consent it must release the tenant from the lease on the tenant's request on 30 days' notice (release is the tenant's sole remedy). If consent is reasonably withheld, no release.
atoms.quote: a tenant renting a residence may not assign his lease without the written consent of the owner, which consent may be unconditionally withheld without cause provided that the owner shall release the tenant from the lease upon request of the tenant upon thirty days notice if the owner unreasonably withholds consent which release shall be the sole remedy of the tenant.
atoms.cross_time: An early-termination route that ends rent liability 30 days after a release request.

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 7
atoms.effective_from: in force at retrieval 2026-09-28; enactment date not read
atoms.condition: Tenant under an existing lease in a building of four or more residential units requests consent to sublet by certified mail with the listed information.
atoms.effect: Landlord may not unreasonably withhold consent; silence for 30 days after the request (or after requested additional information) is deemed consent. If consent is given, the tenant remains liable on the lease. If consent is reasonably withheld, no sublet and no release.
atoms.quote: Landlord's failure to send such a notice shall be deemed to be a consent to the proposed subletting. If the landlord consents, the premises may be sublet in accordance with the request, but the tenant thereunder, shall nevertheless remain liable for the performance of tenant's obligations under said lease.

judgment_terms: units for which there are constitutional or statutory criteria covering admission
atoms.quote: they shall not apply to public housing and other units for which there are constitutional or statutory criteria covering admission thereto nor to a proprietary lease
