atoms.effect: A default judgment application must include the consumer-debt proof the amended 3215(f) and (j) require, including a statement that the 2% consumer-debt interest rate applies (NY:CPLR-5004(a)-consumer-2pct), in addition to the 3215(g)(3) mailing (NY:CPLR-3215(g)(3)).
atoms.quote: a statement that the interest rate for consumer debt
atoms.reasoning: Section 17 of the bill amends 3215(f) and (j) for consumer debt actions.

atoms.instrument: NY Limited Liability Company Law
atoms.condition: The owner is a limited liability company formed outside New York that is doing business in New York (for example regularly leasing NYC units), and it, or a collector in its name, sues a former tenant.
atoms.effect: It cannot maintain the suit until it holds a New York certificate of authority; the suit is dismissed on motion until it does. The defect is curable and does not affect the lease, the deposit statement or its defense of a tenant's suit. A nonresident owner may be required to post security for costs (CPLR 8501(a)). Suing, defending, settling claims and keeping bank accounts are not doing business (NY:LLC-803-doing-business-exclusions); whether owning and regularly leasing New York units is doing business is a judgment on the regularity of the owner's New York activity.
atoms.quote: may not maintain any action, suit or special proceeding in any court of this state unless and until such limited liability company shall have received a certificate of authority in this state.

construction.quote: does not impair the validity of any contract or act of the foreign limited liability company
properly denied that branch of the defendant's cross-motion which was to require the plaintiff to post a bond as security for costs

(a) Without excluding other activities that may not constitute doing business in this state, a foreign limited liability company shall not be considered to be doing business in this state for the purposes of this chapter, by reason of carrying on in this state any one or more of the following activities: (1) maintaining or defending any action or proceeding, whether judicial, administrative, arbitrative or otherwise or effecting settlement thereof or the settlement of claims or disputes;

atoms.reasoning: 808(a) bars the action until authority is obtained; 808(b) keeps contracts valid and permits defense. S. Garson (2d Dept 2026) applied 808(a) and CPLR 8501(a) to a landlord LLC.

atoms.instrument: NY Business Corporation Law
atoms.condition: The owner is a corporation formed outside New York that is doing business in New York, and it, or a collector in its name, sues a former tenant.
atoms.effect: It cannot maintain the suit until it is authorized to do business in New York and has paid the fees and taxes the section requires; the defect is curable and does not affect its contracts or its defense of a tenant's suit. Suing, defending, settling claims and keeping bank accounts are not doing business (NY:BCL-1301-doing-business-and-fictitious-name); whether owning and leasing New York units is doing business is a judgment on the regularity of that activity.
atoms.quote: shall not maintain any action or special proceeding in this state unless and until such corporation has been authorized to do business in this state

construction.quote: (b) Without excluding other activities which may not constitute doing business in this state, a foreign corporation shall not be considered to be doing business in this state, for the purposes of this chapter, by reason of carrying on in this state any one or more of the following activities: (1) Maintaining or defending any action or proceeding, whether judicial, administrative, arbitrative or otherwise, or effecting settlement thereof or the settlement of claims or disputes.

atoms.reasoning: BCL 1301(b) lists acts that are not doing business, so only the remaining activity is weighed.

atoms.instrument: NY Multiple Dwelling Law art. 7-C
atoms.condition: The unit is in an interim multiple dwelling covered by, or registered with, the Loft Board (MDL art. 7-C), and the occupant is protected by the article.
atoms.effect: Outside this engine: Step 0 routes the unit to the operator. Rent recovery from a protected occupant turns on the owner's compliance with article 7-C, not on MDL 302 or 325(2).
atoms.quote: provided that he is in compliance with this article.

atoms.instrument: NY Limited Liability Company Law
atoms.condition: The owner is a New York LLC that has not filed proof of publication (LLC Law 206) within 120 days of formation, and it, or a collector in its name, sues a former tenant.
atoms.effect: Its authority to carry on business is suspended and it cannot maintain the action; the action is dismissed on motion if it has not cured. Filing the proof of publication at any time annuls the suspension. The defect is not jurisdictional, may be cured after commencement, and does not affect the lease, the deposit statement or the LLC's defense of a tenant's suit. Operator step: confirm the publication filing before suing.
atoms.quote: Failure to comply with these requirements precludes a limited liability company from maintaining any action or special proceeding in New York

construction.quote: such suspension of such limited liability company's authority to carry on, conduct or transact business shall be annulled.
constitute a jurisdictional defect requiring dismissal

atoms.reasoning: The Appellate Division, Second Department (Small Step Day Care, 2016) holds that an LLC that has not complied cannot maintain an action and affirmed dismissal; no Appellate Division decision holds otherwise, so it binds every trial court. 1700 First Ave (App Term 1st) held only that the defect is not jurisdictional, which is consistent. LLC Law 206(a) annuls the suspension on filing.

atoms.instrument: NYC Civil Court Act art. 18-A
atoms.condition: An owner that is a corporation, partnership, association or LLC wants to sue a former tenant in the commercial claims part.
atoms.effect: It may do so only if its principal office is in New York State and, when the claim is filed, the former tenant resides, has an office or is regularly employed in New York City; the claim is money only, up to the small claims maximum ($10,000, CCA 1801), exclusive of interest and costs. If either condition fails, the commercial claims part is not available.
atoms.quote: the claimant is a corporation, partnership or association, which has its principal office in the state of New York and provided that the defendant either resides, or has an office for the transaction of business or a regular employment, within the city of New York.

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law art. 29-HHH (coerced debt)
atoms.condition: A natural-person former tenant tells the landlord, its manager or a collector that all or part of a lease balance is coerced debt: incurred for household purposes because of duress, intimidation, threat, force, coercion, manipulation or undue influence by an intimate partner or a family or household member (or in the other relationships 604-aa(3) lists). Branch (a): the tenant gives a statement that the debt is coerced and adequate documentation (a police report, a law-enforcement report, a court order, or another document 604-aa(2) lists). Branch (b): the tenant notifies, orally or in writing, without documentation, or with insufficient documentation.
atoms.effect: (a) Within ten business days: stop collection on that debt until the review is complete. Within thirty business days: complete a review of the tenant's information and the file, without contacting the person accused of the coercion, using only the contact details the tenant gave, and without disclosing the documents. Within five business days after the review: if collection resumes, send the written determination, its good-faith basis and notice of the right to request reconsideration; if it does not, tell the tenant in writing. (b) Send the tenant the written notice with the statutory text of 604-bb(2)(a). The 14-day deposit statement is still sent on time: it itemizes the account but does not demand the disputed part while collection is stopped. A person who itself did the coercing is not a 'creditor'. The statute's duties to tell a consumer reporting agency that the account is disputed and to correct reporting do not bind a furnisher: FCRA 1681t(b)(1)(F) displaces state requirements on furnishing (US:15USC1681t(b)(1)(F)-furnisher-preemption), and the federal dispute and accuracy duties govern how the account is reported (US:15USC1681s-2(a)(3), US:15USC1681s-2(a)(1)(A)).
atoms.quote: 1. Within ten business days of receipt of the following, a creditor shall cease collection activities until completion of the review under subdivision three of this section: (a) adequate documentation of coerced debt; and (b) the debtor's statement that a particular debt being collected, or portion thereof, is coerced debt.

construction.quote: 3. "Coerced debt" means a debt arising out of a transaction primarily for personal, family or household purposes that was incurred because of duress, intimidation, threat, force, coercion, manipulation, or undue influence within the context of intimate relationships or relationships between family or household members

3. (a) Within ten business days of receiving all the information required under subdivision one of this section, the creditor shall, if such creditor furnishes adverse information about the debtor to a consumer reporting agency, notify such consumer reporting agency that the account is disputed.
(b) Within thirty business days of receiving all the information required under subdivision one of this section, the creditor shall complete a review
If a debtor notifies a creditor, either orally or in writing, that a debt is a coerced debt but does not provide the documentation required in subdivision one of this section
No requirement or prohibition may be imposed under the laws of any State—

atoms.reasoning: Article 29-HHH defines coerced debt by the household purpose of the transaction, with no credit element, so it reaches a residential lease balance, unlike art. 29-H (NY:ADJ-lease-balance-not-consumer-credit). 'Creditor' includes the person owed and any debt collector. GOL 7-108 still requires the itemized statement within 14 days; itemizing without demanding the disputed part meets both duties. The credit-reporting branch of 604-bb is a state requirement on the subject matter of 1681s-2(a)(3) and (a)(8), which 1681t(b)(1)(F) displaces; stopping collection, the review and the determinations are collection conduct and stand.

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law art. 29-HHH (coerced debt)
atoms.condition: The landlord or a collector sues a natural-person former tenant for a lease balance, or the tenant, after requesting reconsideration of a decision to resume collection, sues the creditor.
atoms.effect: That all or part of the balance is coerced debt is an affirmative defense to the landlord's suit. The tenant may also bring an action for a declaratory judgment that the debt is coerced once it has requested reconsideration under 604-bb(4) and the creditor affirmed its decision; the person accused of the coercion is not a necessary party.
atoms.quote: 4. In any action by a creditor against a debtor to collect a debt, it shall be an affirmative defense to such action that all or a portion of the debt is coerced debt.

construction.quote: 1. A debtor shall have a cause of action against a creditor in any court having jurisdiction to issue a declaratory judgment establishing that a debt or portion of a debt asserted to be owed to such creditor is a coerced debt.

atoms.reasoning: Section 604-cc(4) makes coercion an affirmative defense in any creditor's action; 604-cc(1) gives the debtor a declaratory action after the reconsideration step.

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act; CPLR 210 (adjudication)
atoms.condition: The tenant (or the last surviving co-tenant) dies before the refund is paid or the balance is collected.
atoms.effect: The refund belongs to the estate. Pay it to the executor or administrator on letters, or, for an estate of personal property of $50,000 or less, to a voluntary administrator on the court's short-form certificate, which discharges the landlord. A landlord's refund is not among the debts SCPA 1310 lets a holder pay without administration, so payment to a relative without letters or a certificate does not discharge the landlord. The statement is still due within 14 days of vacatur: send it to the fiduciary if known, otherwise to the last known address addressed to the tenant's estate (NY:ADJ-provide-address-branches), and hold the refund in trust (NY:GOL-7-103(1)-trust) until a fiduciary presents authority. The landlord's claim against the estate is presented to the fiduciary within 7 months of letters (after that the fiduciary is not chargeable for good-faith payments already made); 18 months after death are not counted in the limitation period against the estate; the estate may bring the tenant's own deposit claim within one year after death if the period had not run. Further branches. One of several co-tenants dies: the estate and the survivors stay jointly liable (NY:GOL-15-106-cotenant-death) and the refund follows NY:ADJ-cotenants-payee. No one eligible for letters: the public administrator takes the refund and receives the claim, before letters if need be, and its receipt in a small estate discharges the landlord (NY:SCPA-1112-public-administrator, NY:SCPA-1118-pa-before-letters, NY:SCPA-1115-pa-small-estate). A tenant domiciled elsewhere: its foreign fiduciary may be paid without a court order (NY:EPTL-13-3.4-foreign-fiduciary), and another state's small-estate certificate is honored on reciprocity (NY:SCPA-1309-foreign-small-estate). The claim is written and states its facts and amount (NY:SCPA-1803-claim-form); it is deemed rejected 90 days after presentation (NY:SCPA-1806-allowance-rejection); presenting it counts as commencement for limitations (NY:SCPA-1808-presentation-tolls); a suit on a rejected claim is due within 60 days, or the claim is tried on the accounting (NY:SCPA-1810-sue-within-60-days). A tenant who had an article 81 guardian: the guardian's authority over the refund ends at death, and the refund goes to the personal representative or the public administrator (NY:MHL-81.44-death-of-ward).
atoms.quote: The delivery by a voluntary administrator to a debtor, transfer agent, safe deposit company, bank, trust company or other person holding or having custody or possession or control of any personal property of the decedent, of the short form certificate of the court, the receipt of the administrator, and the surrender of any evidentiary document, shall constitute a complete release and discharge

construction.quote: A small estate is the estate of a domiciliary or a non-domiciliary who dies leaving personal property having a gross value of $50,000 or less
(a) "Debt" means (i) money or securities payable on account of a deposit in a bank, national bank, trust company, branch of a foreign banking corporation
If any claim is not presented within 7 months from the date of issue of letters, the fiduciary shall not be chargeable for any assets or moneys that he may have paid in good faith

The period of eighteen months after the death, within or without the state, of a person against whom a cause of action exists is not a part of the time within which the action must be commenced against his executor or administrator.
an action may be commenced by his representative within one year after his death.
On the death of a joint obligor in contract, his estate shall be bound as such jointly and severally with the surviving obligor or obligors.
If the fiduciary shall fail to allow the claim within 90 days from the date that it has been presented to him, the claim shall be deemed to have been rejected.

atoms.reasoning: The deposit is the tenant's money (GOL 7-103) and passes to the estate. SCPA 1305 makes delivery to a voluntary administrator a complete discharge. SCPA 1310 lists bank deposits, insurance, public payments, wages, pensions and similar debts that may be paid without administration; a landlord's refund is not listed, so the general rule (payment to the fiduciary) governs. SCPA 1802 and CPLR 210 fix the claim and limitation periods.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR
atoms.condition: A party to a claim between the landlord and a former tenant dies before the limitation period runs.
atoms.effect: Against the deceased tenant's executor or administrator, the 18 months after death are not counted. The estate of a deceased tenant may sue within one year after death if the period had not run at death. Payee and claim rules: NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee.
atoms.quote: The period of eighteen months after the death, within or without the state, of a person against whom a cause of action exists is not a part of the time within which the action must be commenced against his executor or administrator.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law
atoms.condition: The former tenant signs a writing acknowledging the lease balance or promising to pay it, or makes a part payment.
atoms.effect: A signed written acknowledgment or promise starts the six-year contract period anew from its date; an oral acknowledgment does not. A part payment keeps its common-law effect of restarting the period. This applies while the lease balance is not a consumer credit transaction (NY:ADJ-lease-balance-not-consumer-credit); a claim under CPLR 214-i cannot be revived.
atoms.quote: An acknowledgment or promise contained in a writing signed by the party to be charged thereby is the only competent evidence of a new or continuing contract whereby to take an action out of the operation of the provisions of limitations of time

construction.quote: This section does not alter the effect of a payment of principal or interest.

atoms.reasoning: GOL 17-101 requires a signed writing for an acknowledgment and preserves the effect of part payment.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR 203, 213, 214 (adjudication)
atoms.condition: A former tenant sues the landlord over the deposit. Branch (a): punitive damages for a willful violation (GOL 7-108(1-a)(g)), or recovery of an amount the landlord could have kept at common law but lost only by the 14-day forfeiture. Branch (b): return of a deposit kept without a lawful basis (no rent owed, no tenant damage, wear and tear), or actual damages for it.
atoms.effect: (a) Three years from accrual (CPLR 214(2)). (b) Six years from accrual (CPLR 213). The claim accrues when the 14 days end without a compliant statement and refund. Extensions: the tenant's military service is not counted (US:50USC3936-tolling); if the tenant is in bankruptcy, the trustee may sue until the later of the period's end or two years after the order for relief (US:11USC108(a)-debtor-claims); if the tenant died, the representative may sue within one year after death if the period had not run (NY:CPLR-210-death). Operator step: keep the settlement file until the latest of those dates. A plaintiff that resided outside New York when the claim accrued (an owner entity based elsewhere, a tenant who had moved out of state) must also sue within its home state's period, with that state's tolling (NY:CPLR-202-borrowing).
atoms.quote: 2\. an action to recover upon a liability, penalty or forfeiture created or imposed by statute except as provided in sections 213 and 215;

construction.quote: CPLR 214 (2) does not automatically apply to all causes of action in which a statutory remedy is sought, but only where liability “would not exist but for a statute”
computed from the time the cause of action accrued

An action based upon a cause of action accruing without the state cannot be commenced after the expiration of the time limited by the laws of either the state or the place without the state where the cause of action accrued, except that where the cause of action accrued in favor of a resident of the state the time limited by the laws of the state shall apply.

atoms.reasoning: Gaidon (Court of Appeals) confines CPLR 214(2) to liabilities that would not exist but for a statute. The punitive damages and a forfeiture-only recovery exist only by GOL 7-108; a deposit held in trust and wrongly kept is recoverable at common law (NY:COMMONLAW-deposit-return), so the six-year contract period governs it. Time runs from accrual (CPLR 203(a)), which is the end of the statutory 14 days.

judgment_terms: ability to pay materially affected by reason of such service
atoms.instrument: NY Military Law art. 13
atoms.condition: The tenant signed the lease before entering active federal or state military service, and the balance bears interest, fees or other charges above 6% a year.
atoms.effect: During any part of active service the balance may not bear more than 6% a year, 'interest' including service charges, fees and other charges, unless a court on the landlord's application finds the tenant's ability to pay was not materially affected by the service. The federal cap applies alongside it: US:50USC3937-6pct.
atoms.quote: As used in this section the term "interest" includes service charges, renewal charges, fees and any other charges (except bona fide insurance) with respect to such obligation or liability.

construction.quote: in active military service of the organized militia of the state before that person's entry into such service shall, during any part of the period active military service, bear interest at a rate in excess of six percent per year

atoms.reasoning: Section 323-a covers federal and state active service and reaches fees and charges as 'interest'.

judgment_terms: acts so inconsistent with the landlord-tenant relationship
atoms.instrument: NY interpretive authority (case law)
atoms.provision: Riverside Research Inst. v KMGA, Inc., 68 NY2d 689 (1986)
atoms.condition: A tenant with a fixed term leaves early, and the landlord's conduct together with the tenant's is so inconsistent with the landlord-tenant relationship that it shows intent to treat the lease as ended (for example the landlord accepts the keys and occupies, renovates or combines the unit for its own account, or releases the tenant).
atoms.effect: The lease ends on that date and rent stops; the landlord recovers only rent accrued before it and proven damage. Accepting keys for re-letting on the tenant's account, or re-letting under NY:RPL-227-e, is not surrender by operation of law.
atoms.quote: A surrender by operation of law occurs when the parties to a lease both do some act so inconsistent with the landlord-*692tenant relationship that it indicates their intent to deem the lease terminated

construction.quote: Whether a surrender by operation of law has occurred is a determination to be made on the facts.

atoms.reasoning: The Court of Appeals states the test and leaves it to the facts. RPL 227-e requires re-letting efforts on the tenant's behalf, so re-letting under it is not conduct inconsistent with the lease.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR
atoms.condition: The landlord or its collector asks the clerk to enter a default judgment on a former tenant's balance.
atoms.effect: The request carries an affidavit of the plaintiff or its attorney that, after reasonable inquiry, it has reason to believe the limitation period has not expired; without it the clerk does not enter judgment.
atoms.quote: (j) Affidavit. A request for a default judgment entered by the clerk, must be accompanied by an affidavit by the plaintiff or plaintiff's attorney stating that after reasonable inquiry, he or she has reason to believe that the statute of limitations has not expired.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR
atoms.condition: A charge on the final account rests on a clause of a residential lease that the landlord or its agent printed or prepared, and the clause is printed in type under 8 points (5.5 points for upper case) or is not clear and legible.
atoms.effect: The landlord cannot put the clause in evidence, so the charge resting only on it (late fee, lease-break sum, interest, fee clause) is not kept from the deposit or pursued; the tenant may still rely on the clause.
atoms.quote: a lease for space to be occupied for residential purposes where the print is not clear and legible or is less than eight points in depth or five and one-half points in depth for upper case type may not be received in evidence in any trial, hearing or proceeding on behalf of the party who printed or prepared such contract or agreement

atoms.instrument: NY Military Law art. 13
atoms.condition: The landlord seeks a default judgment against a former tenant.
atoms.effect: State law adds no non-military affidavit of its own; the federal affidavit (US:50USC3931(b)(1)) is still required for every default judgment.
atoms.quote: the court shall not require the attorney for the plaintiff or petitioner to submit an affidavit or affirmation that the defendant or respondent is not in military service, provided that the court may impose such requirement where authorized by federal law.

atoms.instrument: NY Department of State regulations (19 NYCRR part 175)
atoms.actor: licensed real estate broker (managing agent; Handoff in a broker configuration)
atoms.condition: A licensed real estate broker receives or holds a tenant's deposit or other money of its principal.
atoms.effect: It may not commingle that money with its own; it deposits it within three business days in a separate, special, federally insured bank account used only for such money, safeguarding it until then, and keeps no interest for itself except as applied to earned commission. A breach is a licensing violation in addition to the GOL 7-103 trust breach (NY:CASE-Paterno-commingling-forfeiture).
atoms.quote: A real estate broker shall not commingle the money or other property of his principal with his own and shall at all times maintain a separate, special bank account

construction.quote: which deposit shall be made within three business days
Said monies shall not be placed in any depository, fund or investment other than a federally insured bank account.

atoms.reasoning: The regulation governs every licensed broker holding a principal's money, which includes a tenant's deposit held for the owner.

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 7
atoms.condition: The ledger shows a payment, fee or charge demanded for an application or before or at the start of the tenancy, other than the deposit, rent and a background or credit check within RPL 238-a(1)(b).
atoms.effect: It was unlawful: it is not charged on the final account or kept from the deposit, and if the tenant paid it, the tenant may recover it, so it is credited against any balance. A background or credit check fee above the lesser of actual cost or $20, or charged without giving the tenant the check and receipt the section requires, is treated the same. Waivers are void (NY:RPL-238-a(3)).
atoms.quote: or demand any other payment, fee or charge before or at the beginning of the tenancy, except background checks and credit checks as provided by paragraph (b) of this subdivision

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law
atoms.condition: The landlord seeks the balance from a person other than the tenant who promised to answer for it (a guarantor).
atoms.effect: Only on a guaranty in a writing subscribed by the guarantor or its lawful agent; an oral guaranty is void. An individual guarantor is a person obligated to pay the debt and is protected by the federal and city collection rules like the tenant (US:15USC1692a(3)); in the tenant's chapter 13 case the co-debtor stay protects an individual guarantor (US:11USC1301-codebtor-stay).
atoms.quote: Every agreement, promise or undertaking is void, unless it or some note or memorandum thereof be in writing, and subscribed by the party to be charged therewith, or by his lawful agent

construction.quote: 2\. Is a special promise to answer for the debt, default or miscarriage of another person;

atoms.reasoning: GOL 5-701(a)(2) brings a promise to answer for another's debt within the writing requirement.

judgment_terms: discriminate in the terms, conditions or privileges
atoms.instrument: NY Executive Law art. 15 (Human Rights Law)
atoms.condition: Any settlement decision on a New York tenancy: what is deducted, how strictly damage is assessed, whether a balance is pursued, reported or written off. Not a building of two units or fewer where the owner lives in one, or a room in the owner's or occupant's own housing accommodation.
atoms.effect: The same standard applies to every tenant; it may not vary because of race, creed, color, national origin, citizenship or immigration status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, military status, sex, age, disability, marital status, status as a victim of domestic violence, lawful source of income or familial status.
atoms.quote: (2) To discriminate against any person because of race, creed, color, national origin, citizenship or immigration status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, military status, sex, age, disability, marital status, status as a victim of domestic violence, lawful source of income or familial status in the terms, conditions or privileges of the sale, rental or lease of any such housing accommodation

construction.quote: to the rental of a housing accommodation in a building which contains housing accommodations for not more than two families living independently of each other, if the owner resides in one of such housing accommodations

atoms.reasoning: Deposit deductions, damage assessment and collection are terms, conditions or privileges of the rental. Section 296(5)(a)(4) exempts the owner-occupied two-family building and room rentals.

atoms.condition: The tenant or a family member is a victim of domestic violence.
atoms.effect: The owner, manager or agent may not discriminate in the terms, conditions or privileges of the rental because of that status, including in deductions, collection and reporting at move-out. The early-termination right and its settlement rules are in NY:RPL-227-c(1).
atoms.quote: (2) discriminate in the terms, conditions, or privileges of any such rental

atoms.instrument: NY RPAPL art. 13
atoms.condition: The building is sold in foreclosure (or ownership passes during it) while a tenant of a unit not subject to rent control or stabilization is in occupancy under a lease or an oral or implied rental agreement.
atoms.effect: The successor takes subject to the tenant's right to stay for the greater of 90 days from its notice or (b) the rest of the lease, if the tenant occupied when the foreclosure began or received the RPAPL 1303 notice, or (c) the rest of a lease entered later, up to three years; a lease qualifies only if the tenant is not the owner and the rent is not substantially below fair market rent (unless the unit is subsidized); a successor that will occupy one unsubsidized unit as its primary residence may limit that unit to 90 days. The tenancy continues on the terms in effect at the judgment or transfer, and must give written notice of that right and of its name and address. Rent for the continued tenancy is owed to the successor (NY:RPL-223); the settlement at move-out is the successor's (NY:GOL-7-105(1)). The federal 90-day notice floor for a bona fide tenant is met by the state right.
atoms.quote: a tenant of a unit not subject to rent control or rent stabilization shall have the right to remain in occupancy of the unit of the subject residential real property

construction.quote: a period of ninety days from the date of the service of such notice; or (b) for the remainder of the lease term
shall notify all tenants of its name and address
the provision, by such successor in interest of a notice to vacate to any bona fide tenant at least 90 days before the effective date of such notice
provided that if a successor in interest who acquires title to such residential real property intends to occupy a single unit as his or her primary residence
up to a maximum of three years
such lease must require the payment of rent for such unit that is not substantially less than the fair market rent for the unit

atoms.reasoning: RPAPL 1305 gives the market-rate tenant the longer of 90 days or the lease remainder on unchanged terms; the federal Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act sets a 90-day floor that the state right equals or exceeds.

atoms.instrument: NYC Civil Court Act art. 18
atoms.condition: A former tenant holds a recorded NYC small-claims judgment against the landlord arising from its trade or business, at least two other unsatisfied small-claims judgments arise from the same business, and the landlord does not pay within 30 days after notice given as the section requires.
atoms.effect: The tenant may sue for three times the judgment, reasonable counsel fees, costs and disbursements. The only defense is that the landlord lacked resources to pay within the 30 days.
atoms.quote: the judgment creditor shall be entitled to commence an action against said judgment debtor for treble the amount of such unsatisfied judgment, together with reasonable counsel fees

atoms.instrument: NYC Civil Court Act art. 18
atoms.condition: A former tenant of NYC property sues the owner over the tenancy (the deposit, rent paid, damages) for $10,000 or less exclusive of interest and costs.
atoms.effect: The tenant may bring it in the NYC small claims part even if the owner neither lives nor does business in the city.
atoms.quote: or where claimant is a tenant or lessee of real property owned by the defendant and the claim relates to such tenancy or lease, and such real property is situated within the city of New York.

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law art. 29-H
atoms.actor: landlord (principal creditor); managing agent; collection agency
atoms.condition: Collecting a former tenant's balance, including from or through the tenant's family or heirs.
atoms.effect: No one may represent that a family member must pay the tenant's debt in a way the FDCPA forbids, or misrepresent a family member's obligation to pay it (for example telling a parent or the heirs they owe it).
atoms.quote: the principal creditors and/or debt collection agencies shall not make any misrepresentation about the family member's obligation to pay such debts.
atoms.reasoning: Section 601-a is not limited to 'consumer claims' under GBL 600(1), so it reaches a lease balance.

construction.quote: No principal creditors and/or debt collection agencies shall make any representation that a person is required to pay the debt of a family member

atoms.instrument: NYS Comptroller, Office of Unclaimed Funds, Property Type Table
atoms.condition: A licensed real estate company (managing agent) holds a former tenant's unclaimed refund in its escrow account.
atoms.effect: It reports under TR04 Escrow Accounts (held by real estate companies), with a 3-year dormancy. An owner or a manager that is not a real estate company holding the refund reports under MS11 (NY:OSC-MS11-refunds-due).
atoms.quote: TR04 1315 Escrow Accounts (held by real estate companies) 3 years

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law art. 39-F (SHIELD Act)
atoms.condition: A person or business owns or licenses computerized data including a New York resident's private information, such as a bank account number with the access code used for an electronic refund.
atoms.effect: It develops, implements and maintains reasonable administrative, technical and physical safeguards for that data, including secure disposal when the settlement no longer needs it. A small business's safeguards are measured by its size and the sensitivity of the data.
atoms.quote: Any person or business that owns or licenses computerized data which includes private information of a resident of New York shall develop, implement and maintain reasonable safeguards to protect the security, confidentiality and integrity of the private information including, but not limited to, disposal of data.

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 7
atoms.condition: The owner has three or fewer rental units and signs a residential lease.
atoms.effect: Before signing, it gives the tenant a conspicuous bold notice whether any certificate of occupancy the law requires is currently valid for the unit, or a copy of the valid certificate; a waiver is void. The notice is evidence of the unit's status when rent for an unlawful period is later disputed (NY:MDL-302(1)(b)).
atoms.quote: the owner of real property consisting of three or fewer rental units shall provide conspicuous notice in bold face type as to whether a certificate of occupancy, if such certificate is required by law, is currently valid for the dwelling unit subject to the lease or rental

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law 7-108 (adjudication); E-SIGN 15 U.S.C. 7001(c)
atoms.condition: The landlord provides the 14-day itemized statement by email or text message.
atoms.effect: The statement is provided on the day it is sent to a known email address or phone number; the tenant's E-SIGN consent is not a condition, because 7-108(1-a)(e) requires an 'itemized statement' without requiring it 'in writing', and the writing requirement the courts read into it is met by email or text. The refund is a payment, not information, and goes by a means directed to the tenant (NY:ADJ-provide-address-branches). Inspection notices under (1-a)(d) are 'in writing' notices and follow US:15USC7001(c)-esign-consent.
atoms.quote: the landlord shall provide the tenant with an itemized statement indicating the basis for the amount of the deposit retained, if any, and shall return any remaining portion of the deposit to the tenant

construction.quote: whether by letter, email, text, or any other written means

(c) Consumer disclosures (1) Consent to electronic records Notwithstanding subsection (a), if a statute, regulation, or other rule of law requires that information relating to a transaction or transactions in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce be provided or made available to a consumer in writing, the use of an electronic record to provide or make available (whichever is required) such information satisfies the requirement that such information be in writing if- (A) the consumer has affirmatively consented to such use and has not withdrawn such consent;

atoms.reasoning: E-SIGN 7001(c) applies where a rule of law requires information 'in writing'. Subdivision (1-a)(e) uses no writing words, unlike (1-a)(c) and (d). The only rule that makes the statement a writing is the construction in Bogom-Shanon, which itself holds that email and text are written means, so an emailed or texted statement satisfies the state requirement without resort to E-SIGN.

atoms.effective_from: 2026-02-17 (60th day after L.2025 c.708 became law)
atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law art. 22-A (as amended by L.2025 c.708, FAIR Business Practices Act)
atoms.condition: Any act or practice in leasing to, settling with or collecting from a residential tenant in New York.
atoms.effect: Unfair, abusive and deceptive acts are unlawful. Unfair: causes or is likely to cause substantial injury not reasonably avoidable and not outweighed by benefits. Abusive: materially interferes with the tenant's understanding of a term, or takes unreasonable advantage of the tenant's lack of understanding, inability to protect its interests, or reasonable reliance. The Attorney General enforces all three. A tenant injured by a deceptive act may sue for actual damages or $50, whichever is greater, increased up to three times actual damages up to $1,000 for a willful or knowing violation, plus attorney's fees. Every charge and collection message is tested against these standards.
atoms.reasoning: L.2025 c.708 rewrote 349(a) to reach unfair and abusive practices and took effect on its 60th day; the private action in 349(h) remains limited to deceptive acts.
atoms.quote: (a) Unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices in the conduct of any business, trade or commerce or in the furnishing of any service in this state are hereby declared unlawful.

construction.quote: (h) In addition to the right of action granted to the attorney general pursuant to this section, any person who has been injured by reason of any deceptive act or deceptive practice made unlawful by this section may bring an action in such person’s own name to enjoin such deceptive act or deceptive practice, an action to recover such person’s actual damages or fifty dollars, whichever is greater, or both such actions.
§ 6. This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall 29 have become a law.

judgment_terms: intent and primary purpose of bringing a lawsuit
atoms.instrument: NY Judiciary Law
atoms.condition: A former tenant's balance is assigned or sold to Handoff, an affiliate, a collection business or any corporation. Branch (a): the assignee takes it with the intent and primary purpose of suing on it. Branch (b): the owner keeps the claim and the collector acts as agent, any suit being the owner's.
atoms.effect: (a) The assignment is champertous unless the assignee paid or is bound to pay an aggregate purchase price of at least $500,000 for the claims; the assignee cannot maintain the action, and a corporation faces a fine of up to $5,000 (a person, a misdemeanor). (b) Section 489 does not apply. An assignee is also barred from small claims (NY:CCA-1809(1)).
atoms.reasoning: Justinian (Court of Appeals 2016) reads 489 to bar purchases made with the intent and primary purpose of suing, and requires the safe-harbor price to be binding.
atoms.quote: 1. No person or co-partnership, engaged directly or indirectly in the business of collection and adjustment of claims, and no corporation or association, directly or indirectly, itself or by or through its officers, agents or employees, shall solicit, buy or take an assignment of, or be in any manner interested in buying or taking an assignment of a bond, promissory note, bill of exchange, book debt, or other thing in action, or any claim or demand, with the intent and for the purpose of bringing an action or proceeding thereon

construction.quote: As pertinent here, the statute prohibits the purchase of notes, securities, or other instruments or claims with the intent and for the primary purpose of bringing a lawsuit (see id.

judgment_terms: dangerous, hazardous or detrimental to life or health
atoms.instrument: NY Social Services Law
atoms.condition: During the period claimed the former tenant received public assistance toward rent, and the enforcing agency reported to the social services department a violation of law relating to dangerous, hazardous or health-detrimental conditions in the building.
atoms.effect: No money judgment for rent is available for any period while the violation was outstanding (until the landlord proves it was corrected), so that rent is not kept from the deposit and is not pursued. Rent after correction and damage claims are unaffected.
atoms.quote: (b) In any such action or proceeding the plaintiff or landlord shall not be entitled to an order or judgment awarding him possession of the premises or providing for removal of the tenant, or to a money judgment against the tenant, on the basis of non-payment of rent for any period during which there was outstanding any violation of law relating to dangerous or hazardous conditions or conditions detrimental to life or health.

atoms.instrument: NY RPAPL; NYC Admin. Code 26-521 to 26-523
atoms.condition: The occupant has lawfully occupied the unit 30 consecutive days or longer or has a lease, and has not surrendered (returned keys or otherwise unequivocally given up occupancy) or abandoned the unit.
atoms.effect: No one may change the lock, remove the occupant's belongings, remove the door or otherwise exclude the occupant except under a warrant of eviction, a court order or a governmental vacate order. Each violation is a class A misdemeanor and a civil penalty of $1,000 to $10,000 under state and city law, and the occupant may recover treble damages (RPAPL 853). Once surrender or abandonment is established, re-entry is lawful and belongings follow NY:COMMONLAW-belongings-abandonment; the 14-day clock runs from that vacatur.

construction.quote: Such person shall also be subject to a civil penalty of not less than one thousand nor more than ten thousand dollars for each violation.

If a person is disseized, ejected, or put out of real property in a forcible or unlawful manner, or, after he has been put out, is held and kept out by force or by putting him in fear of personal violence or by unlawful means, he is entitled to recover treble damages in an action therefor against the wrong-doer.

atoms.reasoning: RPAPL 768 and Admin. Code 26-521 protect any 30-day or leased occupant until lawful process; RPAPL 853 gives treble damages for an unlawful ouster.
atoms.quote: (b) Such person shall also be subject to a civil penalty of not less than one thousand nor more than ten thousand dollars for each violation.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law
atoms.condition: The landlord or its collector releases or settles with one of several jointly liable co-tenants or a guarantor.
atoms.effect: With an express reservation of rights against the others, they stay liable for the balance, reduced by the amount paid and as 15-104 provides. Without it, the claim against each other co-obligor is satisfied to the amount the landlord knew or had reason to know the released one was bound, as between them, to pay, or, without that knowledge, to the lesser of the released obligor's fractional share or what it was bound to pay. Every settlement with one co-tenant states whether rights against the others are reserved.
atoms.quote: Section 15-104 Discharge of one obligor, with reservations Subject to the provisions of section 15-103, the obligee’s release or discharge of one or more of several obligors, or of one or more of joint, or of joint and several obligors shall not discharge co-obligors, against whom the obligee in writing and as part of the same transaction as the release or discharge, expressly reserves his rights; and in the absence of such a reservation of rights shall discharge co-obligors only to the extent provided in section 15-105.

construction.quote: 1. If an obligee releasing or discharging an obligor without express reservation of rights against a co-obligor, then knows or has reason to know that the obligor released or discharged did not pay so much of the claim as he was bound by his contract or relation with that co-obligor to pay, the obligee’s claim against that co-obligor shall be satisfied to the amount which the obligee knew or had reason to know that the released or discharged obligor was bound to such co-obligor to pay. 2. If an obligee so releasing or discharging an obligor has not then such knowledge or reason to know, the obligee’s claim against the co-obligor shall be satisfied to the extent of the lesser of two amounts, namely (a) the amount of the fractional share of the obligor released or discharged, or (b) the amount that such obligor was bound by his contract or relation with the co-obligor to pay.

atoms.reasoning: Section 15-104 preserves claims against co-obligors when the release expressly reserves them; 15-105 fixes the reduction when it does not.

atoms.instrument: NY Uniform Commercial Code art. 1; GOL 15-501
atoms.condition: A former tenant tenders less than the claimed balance on the condition that it be accepted in full satisfaction of a disputed balance.
atoms.effect: Accepting it with an explicit reservation of rights ('without prejudice', 'under protest' or like words, endorsed on the check or stated in writing at acceptance) preserves the claim to the rest. Accepting it without a reservation discharges the rest by accord and satisfaction. A written promise to accept a stated future performance in satisfaction is an enforceable executory accord.
atoms.reasoning: Horn Waterproofing (Court of Appeals 1985) holds that UCC 1-207, now 1-308, lets a creditor keep its claim by depositing a full-payment check under an explicit reservation.
atoms.quote: A party that with explicit reservation of rights performs or promises performance or assents to performance in a manner demanded or offered by the other party does not thereby prejudice the rights reserved. Such words as “without prejudice,” “under protest,” or the like are sufficient.

construction.quote: Uniform Commercial Code § 1-207 changed the law of accord and satisfaction in the case of a party who indorses a full payment check under protest.

2. An executory accord shall not be denied effect as a defense or as the basis of an action or counterclaim by reason of the fact that the satisfaction or discharge of the claim, cause of action, contract, obligation, lease, mortgage or other security interest which is the subject of the accord was to occur at a time after the makin

atoms.instrument: NY Public Service Commission regulations
atoms.condition: The final account carries electricity the landlord billed to the unit through submeters, or another charge described as a utility charge.
atoms.effect: Submetered electricity is a lawful charge (and may be kept from the deposit under NY:GOL-7-108(1-a)(b)-refundable) only if the building's submetering is and continues to be authorized by PSC order where one is required and is consistent with that order and Part 96. Otherwise it is not charged or kept. A flat 'utility fee' for a service not metered to the unit is a fee (NY:ADJ-no-fee-retention). An authorized charge is still capped at the utility's direct-metered residential rate for the same period (NY:16NYCRR-96.1(i)-rate-cap) and is billed and collected only on the conditions of 96.6, including every HEFPA protection before any collection of overdue electric charges (NY:16NYCRR-96.6-submeter-charge-limits).
atoms.quote: (1) Electric service shall only be provided to a multi-unit residential premises in which individual dwelling units in the premises receive submetered electric service if the submetering (i) is and continues to be authorized by commission order where a commission order was necessary

construction.quote: (c) a condition that the submeterer shall not charge more than the applicable rate cap and that, in the event of charges greater than the applicable rate cap, the submeterer may be directed to provide credits to residents for such overcharges plus interest as consistent with Public Service Law section 118 and Part 145 of this Title;

atoms.reasoning: Part 96 caps submetered charges at the rate cap (96.1(i)) and conditions billing and collection on the protections of 96.6, including HEFPA's.

atoms.instrument: NY RPAPL
atoms.condition: A summary proceeding (holdover or nonpayment) preceded the move-out.
atoms.effect: Amounts payable when the proceeding began that the judgment did not award, and the reasonable value of use and occupancy to the date the warrant issued for periods without a rent term, may be pursued by separate action. Use and occupancy is awarded in the proceeding only if the notice of petition demanded it. After the warrant, only use and occupancy for any continued occupation accrues.
atoms.quote: Petitioner may recover by action any sum of money which was payable at the time when the special proceeding was commenced and the reasonable value of the use and occupation to the time when the warrant was issued, for any period of time with respect to which the agreement does not make any provision for payment of rent.

construction.quote: 5. State the relief sought. The relief may include a judgment for rent due, and for a period of occupancy during which no rent is due, for the fair value of use and occupancy of the premises if the notice of petition contains a notice that a demand for such a judgment has been made.

atoms.reasoning: RPAPL 749(3) preserves a separate action for sums payable at commencement and use and occupancy to the warrant; 741(5) conditions use and occupancy in the proceeding on the demand in the notice of petition.

atoms.instrument: NY Multiple Dwelling Law
atoms.condition: During the tenancy the owner failed to have fuel oil supplied to the multiple dwelling, and the tenant, alone or with others, paid for a delivery after substantially complying with the section's steps (reasonable efforts to reach the owner and its normal supplier, a supplier regularly in the business, a price within the department's index).
atoms.effect: The tenant's payment, as the statute allocates it, is deductible from rent: the move-out account credits it, and rent claimed for those months is reduced by it.
atoms.quote: Any payment so made shall be deductible from rent providing the following provisions have been substantially complied with by the tenant or someone acting on his behalf

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law art. 39-F
atoms.condition: A tenant's private information held by the owner, manager or Handoff is, or is reasonably believed to have been, accessed or acquired without authorization.
atoms.effect: Notify each affected resident in the most expedient time possible and within 30 days after discovery (a law-enforcement delay excepted), with the content the section requires, and notify the state agencies it lists; a service provider holding the data for the owner notifies the owner immediately. Failure exposes the business to Attorney General penalties.
atoms.quote: The disclosure shall be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, provided that such notification shall be made within thirty days after the breach has been discovered, except for the legitimate needs of law enforcement, as provided in subdivision four of this section.

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 7
atoms.condition: Within a year before the landlord serves a non-renewal notice or notice to quit or starts a proceeding, the tenant made a good-faith complaint to a governmental authority or in writing to the landlord about a violation or habitability, or took part in a tenants' organization. Not an owner-occupied dwelling of fewer than four units.
atoms.effect: The tenant's showing raises a rebuttable presumption that the landlord's act is retaliatory; a retaliating landlord is liable for damages, fees and costs and may be enjoined. Operator step: record the non-retaliatory reason before serving the notice.
atoms.quote: 5. In an action or proceeding instituted against a tenant of premises or a unit to which this section is applicable, a rebuttable presumption that the landlord is acting in retaliation shall be created if the tenant establishes that the landlord served a notice to quit, or instituted an action or proceeding to recover possession, or attempted to substantially alter the terms of the tenancy, within one year after: a.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law
atoms.condition: Landlord and tenant agree that a lease for a term over one year ends before its date, or change its terms orally where the lease bars oral change.
atoms.effect: The early termination is effective only in a writing signed by the landlord or its agent authorized in writing, or by a surrender by operation of law (NY:CASE-Riverside-surrender-by-operation); an oral agreement alone does not stop rent. Where the lease bars oral change, an unexecuted oral change is unenforceable. Rent stops on the effective surrender date.
atoms.reasoning: GOL 5-703(1) requires a signed writing to surrender a lease for more than a year; 15-301(1) enforces a no-oral-modification clause against an executory oral change. Surrender by operation of law is outside both.
atoms.quote: An estate or interest in real property, other than a lease for a term not exceeding one year, or any trust or power, over or concerning real property, or in any manner relating thereto, cannot be created, granted, assigned, surrendered or declared, unless by act or operation of law, or by a deed or conveyance in writing, subscribed by the person creating, granting, assigning, surrendering or declaring the same, or by his lawful agent, thereunto authorized by writing.

construction.quote: 1. A written agreement or other written instrument which contains a provision to the effect that it cannot be changed orally, cannot be changed by an executory agreement unless such executory agreement is in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement of the change is sought or by his agent.

atoms.instrument: NY General Obligations Law
atoms.condition: After the balance accrued, the former tenant signs a writing promising to waive, extend or not plead the statute of limitations (for example in a payment plan); or the lease itself, made before accrual, contains such a promise.
atoms.effect: A post-accrual signed promise is effective for the period the statute allows from the promise; a promise made before the cause of action accrued, such as a lease clause, has no effect.
atoms.quote: 1. A promise to waive, to extend, or not to plead the statute of limitation applicable to an action arising out of a contract express or implied in fact or in law, if made after the accrual of the cause of action and made, either with or without consideration, in a writing signed by the promisor or his agent is effective, according to its terms, to prevent interposition of the defense of the statute of limitation in an action or proceeding commenced within the time that would be applicable if the cause of action had arisen at the date of the promise, or within such shorter time as may be provided in the promise.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR; Judiciary Law; NYC Civil Court Act
atoms.condition: The owner sues a former tenant for the balance, or a former tenant sues a corporate owner in the small claims part.
atoms.effect: (a) An owner who is a natural person may appear in person or by attorney. (b) An owner that is a corporation, LLC or partnership appears by a licensed attorney, except that in the commercial claims part a corporation may appear by its own authorized officer, director or employee, not by an outside manager or Handoff. (c) Handoff or a manager that is a corporation may prepare evidence for counsel but may not appear, sign pleadings as attorney or hold out legal services for the owner; its individual staff may not either. A violation is a misdemeanor. (d) Sued by a tenant in the small claims part, a corporate owner may defend by an attorney or by its own authorized officer, director or employee, whose appearance binds the corporation (CCA 1809(2)); never by an outside manager or Handoff.
atoms.reasoning: CPLR 321(a) requires a corporation to appear by attorney except where otherwise provided; CCA 1809-A(d) provides otherwise in commercial claims for the corporation's own officers and employees; Judiciary Law 495 and 478 bar corporations and non-lawyers from practising law.
atoms.quote: A party, other than one specified in § 1201 (Representation of infant, incompetent person, or conservatee)section 1201 of this chapter, may prosecute or defend a civil action in person or by attorney, except that a corporation or voluntary association shall appear by attorney, except as otherwise provided in sections 1809 and 1809-A of the New York city civil court act, sections 1809 and 1809-A of the uniform district court act and sections 1809 and 1809-A of the uniform city court act, and except as otherwise provided in section 501 and section 1809 of the uniform justice court act.

construction.quote: 1. No corporation or voluntary association shall (a) practice or appear as an attorney-at-law for any person in any court in this state or before any judicial body, nor (b) make it a business to practice as an attorney-at-law, for any person, in any of said courts

It shall be unlawful for any natural person to practice or appear as an attorney-at-law or as an attorney and counselor-at-law for a person other than himself or herself in a court of record in this state

(d) A corporation may appear as a party in any action brought pursuant to this article by an attorney as well as by any authorized officer, director or employee of the corporation provided that the appearance by a non-lawyer on behalf of a corporation shall be deemed to constitute the requisite authority to bind the corporatio
A corporation may appear in the defense of any small claim action brought pursuant to this article by an attorney as well as by any authorized officer, director or employee of the corporation

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law
atoms.condition: The lease or collection correspondence used a business name other than the owner's legal name.
atoms.effect: Before suing, confirm the assumed-name certificate is on file; without it the action on contracts made in that name cannot be maintained until the certificate is filed. Filing cures; a knowing failure is a misdemeanor. A foreign corporation's fictitious name filed with its application for authority is outside GBL 130, so no assumed-name certificate is needed for leases made in it (NY:BCL-1301-doing-business-and-fictitious-name).
atoms.quote: Any person or persons carrying on, conducting or transacting business as aforesaid who fails to comply with the provisions of this section shall be prohibited from maintaining any action or proceeding in any court in this state on any contract, account or transaction made in a name other than its real name until the certificate required by this section has been executed and filed in accordance with the provisions set forth herein.

construction.quote: (b) Without excluding other activities which may not constitute doing business in this state, a foreign corporation shall not be considered to be doing business in this state, for the purposes of this chapter, by reason of carrying on in this state any one or more of the following activities: (1) Maintaining or defending any action or proceeding, whether judicial, administrative, arbitrative or otherwise, or effecting settlement thereof or the settlement of claims or disputes.

atoms.reasoning: BCL 1301(d) takes a foreign corporation's filed fictitious name outside GBL 130.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR
atoms.condition: A money judgment against a former tenant is fully satisfied.
atoms.effect: Execute and file a satisfaction-piece with the clerk, and mail a copy to the tenant within ten days after filing. For a judgment under $5,000, failing to file within twenty days after full satisfaction subjects the creditor to a $100 penalty.
atoms.quote: (c) When a judgment for less than five thousand dollars is fully satisfied, if the person required to execute and file with the proper clerk pursuant to subdivisions (a) and (d) of this section fails or refuses to do so within twenty days after receiving full satisfaction, then the judgment creditor shall be subject to a penalty of one hundred dollars recoverable by the judgment debtor pursuant to § 7202 (Action by person aggrieved)section seventy-two hundred two of this chapter or article eighteen of either the New York City civil court act, uniform district court act or uniform city court act.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR art. 52; CPLR 211(b)
atoms.condition: The landlord weighs pursuing a balance to judgment against a natural-person former tenant, or enforces one.
atoms.effect: Recovery is limited by (each dollar amount as adjusted every three years under CPLR 5253, the amount in force when the restraint or levy is served governing: NY:CPLR-5253-exemption-adjustment): $2,500 of a bank account being exempt where exempt payments were directly deposited in the 45 days before the restraint, and the further exempt amount of 5222(i); service of the exemption notice and claim forms with every restraining notice; an income execution of no more than ten percent of gross income, subject to the minimum-wage floor; and the presumption that a judgment is paid after twenty years. The expected net recovery for the pursue-or-write-off decision is computed within these limits.
atoms.reasoning: CPLR 5205(l) and 5222(i) exempt account funds; 5222(e) and 5222-a require the exemption notice; 5231(b) caps income executions; 211(b) presumes payment after twenty years.
atoms.quote: then two thousand five hundred dollars in the judgment debtor’s account is exempt from application to the satisfaction of a money judgment.

construction.quote: Except where the provisions of § 5222-A (Service of notices and forms and procedure for claim of exemption)section fifty-two hundred twenty-two-a of this article are applicable, pursuant to subdivision (a) of such section, if a notice in the form prescribed in subdivision (e) of this section has not been given to the judgment debtor or obligor within a year before service of a restraining notice, a copy of the restraining notice together with the notice to judgment debtor or obligor shall be mailed by first class mail or personally delivered to each judgment debtor or obligor who is a natural person within four days of the service of the restraining notice.

Where a judgment debtor is receiving or will receive money from any source, an income execution for installments therefrom of not more than ten percent thereof may be issued and delivered to the sheriff of the county in which the judgment debtor resides or, where the judgment debtor is a non-resident, the county in which he is employed;
A money judgment is presumed to be paid and satisfied after the expiration of twenty years from the time when the party recovering it was first entitled to enforce it.

(a) Beginning on April first, two thousand twelve, and at each three-year interval ending on April first thereafter, the dollar amount of the exemption provided in sections fifty-two hundred five and fifty-two hundred six of this article and sections two hundred eighty-two and two hundred eighty-three of the debtor and creditor law shall be adjusted as provided in subdivision (b) of this section. (b) The superintendent of financial services shall determine the amount of the adjustment based on the change in the consumer price index for all urban consumers, New York-Northern New Jersey-Long Island, NY-NJ-CT-PA, published by the U.S. department of labor, bureau of labor statistics, for the most recent three-year period ending on December thirty-first preceding the adjustment, with each adjusted amount rounded to the nearest twenty-five dollars. (c) Beginning on April first, two thousand twelve, and at each three-year interval ending on April first thereafter, the superintendent of financial services shall publish the current dollar amount of the applicable exemption provided in this article, together with the date of the next scheduled adjustment. The publication shall be substantially in the form set forth below: “Current dollar amount of exemption from application to the satisfaction of money judgments under New York civil practice law and rules sections 5205 and 5206 and exemptions in bankruptcy under debtor and creditor law sections 282 and 283: The following is the current dollar amount of exemptions from the satisfaction of money judgments under civil practice law and rules sections 5205 and 5206 and under debtor and creditor law sections 282 and 283: (amount) This amount is effective on April 1, (year) and shall not apply to cases commenced before April 1, (year). The next adjustment is scheduled for April 1, (year). Such adjustments shall not apply with respect to restraining notices served or executions effected before the date of the adjustment. Nothing in this section limits the judgment debtor’s exemption rights in this section or under any other law.”

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law
atoms.condition: The settlement file (application, identification, bank or card details, SSN) is disposed of.
atoms.effect: Dispose of it only by shredding, destroying the personal identifying information, making it unreadable, or another method consistent with accepted industry practice that the holder reasonably believes prevents unauthorized access.
atoms.quote: shall dispose of a record containing personal identifying information unless the person, business, firm, partnership, association, or corporation, or other person under contract with the business, firm, partnership, association, or corporation does any of the following: a. shreds the record before the disposal of the record; or b. destroys the personal identifying information contained in the record; or c. modifies the record to make the personal identifying information unreadable

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 6-A (Good Cause Eviction)
atoms.condition: A lease or rental agreement term waives or modifies the tenant's Good Cause Eviction rights.
atoms.effect: The term is void.
atoms.quote: Section 218 Waiver of rights void Any agreement by a tenant heretofore or hereinafter entered into in a written lease or other rental agreement waiving or modifying their rights as set forth in this article shall be void as contrary to public policy.

atoms.instrument: NY Real Property Law art. 12-A
atoms.condition: A licensed broker or salesperson mishandles tenant funds or collections (untrustworthiness or incompetency).
atoms.effect: The Department of State may revoke or suspend the licence or impose a fine.
atoms.quote: (a) The department of state may revoke the license of a real estate broker or salesperson or suspend the same, for such period as the department may deem proper, or in lieu thereof may impose a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars payable to the department of state, provided that fifty percent of all moneys received by the department of state for such fines shall be payable to the anti-discrimination in housing fund established pursuant to State Finance Law § 80-A (Anti-discrimination in housing fund)section eighty-a of the state finance law, or a reprimand upon conviction of the licensee of a violation of any provision of this article, or for a violation of subdivision four of § 442-H (Rules of the secretary of state)section four hundred forty-two-h of this article, or for a material misstatement in the application for such license, or if such licensee has been guilty of fraud or fraudulent practices, or for dishonest or misleading advertising, or has demonstrated untrustworthiness or incompetency to act as a real estate broker or salesperson, or for a violation of article fifteen of the executive law committed in their capacity as a real estate broker or salesperson, as the case may be.

atoms.instrument: NY RPAPL
atoms.condition: A summary proceeding to remove a residential tenant.
atoms.effect: The tenant may not be removed because of domestic violence victim status.
atoms.quote: 1. A tenant shall not be removed from possession of a residential unit pursuant to this article because of such person’s domestic violence victim status

atoms.instrument: Uniform Rules for the NYC Civil Court (22 NYCRR 208)
atoms.condition: The landlord brings an RPAPL 711 summary proceeding.
atoms.effect: The petition alleges either that the premises are not a multiple dwelling or that a current HPD registration naming the managing agent is on file.
atoms.quote: In every summary proceeding brought to recover possession of real property pursuant to section 711 of the Real Property Actions and Proceedings Law, the petitioner shall allege either: (1) that the premises are not a multiple dwelling; or (2) that the premises are a multiple dwelling and, pursuant to the Administrative Code, sections 27-2097 _et seq.,_ there is a currently effective registration statement on file

atoms.instrument: NY Multiple Dwelling Law
atoms.condition: The tenant of a multiple dwelling installed its own additional lock on the entrance door.
atoms.effect: No charge may be made or kept for it (a lease term charging additional rent for it is void); the tenant must give the landlord a duplicate key on request.
atoms.quote: every provision of any lease hereafter made or entered into which reserves or provides for the payment by such tenant of any additional rent, bonus, fee or other charge or any other thing of value for the right or privilege of installing and/or maintaining any such lock, shall be deemed to be void as against public policy and wholly unenforceable

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR; Military Law
atoms.condition: Computing the limitation period for a claim between the landlord and a former tenant.
atoms.effect: Also excluded or extended: time a court or statute stayed commencement (204(a)); a timely action dismissed other than by voluntary discontinuance, lack of personal jurisdiction, neglect or a final merits judgment may be recommenced within six months (205(a)); the defendant's continuous absence from the state for four months or more tolls only where jurisdiction could not otherwise be obtained (207); the claimant's infancy or insanity extends its time (208); New York militia service is excluded (Military Law 308).
atoms.reasoning: Each section adds a computation rule alongside CPLR 210, 50 U.S.C. 3936 and 11 U.S.C. 108.
atoms.quote: Where the commencement of an action has been stayed by a court or by statutory prohibition, the duration of the stay is not a part of the time within which the action must be commenced.

construction.quote: If an action is timely commenced and is terminated in any other manner than by a voluntary discontinuance, a failure to obtain personal jurisdiction over the defendant, a dismissal of the complaint for neglect to prosecute the action, or a final judgment upon the merits, the plaintiff, or, if the plaintiff dies, and the cause of action survives, his or her executor or administrator, may commence a new action upon the same transaction or occurrence or series of transactions or occurrences within six months after the termination provided that the new action would have been timely commenced at the time of commencement of the prior action and that service upon defendant is effected within such six-month period.

If, after a cause of action has accrued against a person, that person departs from the state and remains continuously absent therefrom for four months or more, or that person resides within the state under a false name which is unknown to the person entitled to commence the action, the time of his absence or residence within the state under such a false name is not a part of the time within which the action must be commenced.

Civil Practice Law & Rules Section 208 Infancy, insanity (a) If a person entitled to commence an action is under a disability because of infancy or insanity at the time the cause of action accrues, and the time otherwise limited for commencing the action is three years or more and expires no later than three years after the disability ceases, or the person under the disability dies, the time within which the action must be commenced shall be extended to three years after the disability ceases or the person under the disability dies, whichever event first occurs;

The period of military service shall not be included in computing any period now or hereafter to be limited by any law, regulation or order for the bringing of any action or proceeding in any court, board, bureau, commission, department or other agency of government of this state or any of its governmental subdivisions by or against any person in military service, or by or against his heirs, executors, administrators, or assigns, whether such cause of action or the right or privilege to institute such an action or proceeding shall have accrued prior to or during the period of such service, nor shall any part of such period which occurs after the date of enactment of this act be included in computing any period now or hereafter provided by any law for the redemption of real property sold or forfeited to enforce any obligation, tax or assessment.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR
atoms.condition: The former tenant is an infant or adjudicated incompetent, or a party dies, or the judgment debtor dies.
atoms.effect: No default judgment against an infant or adjudicated incompetent unless its representative appeared or twenty days passed after a guardian ad litem's appointment; on a party's death the court substitutes the proper party; after the judgment debtor's death, enforcement needs the surrogate's leave.
atoms.reasoning: CPLR 1203 bars defaults against the listed persons; 1015 requires substitution; 5208 requires leave after death.
atoms.quote: Civil Practice Law & Rules Section 1203 Default judgment No judgment by default may be entered against an infant or a person judicially declared to be incompetent unless his representative appeared in the action or twenty days have expired since appointment of a guardian ad litem for him.

construction.quote: If a party dies and the claim for or against him is not thereby extinguished the court shall order substitution of the proper parties.

Civil Practice Law & Rules Section 5208 Enforcement after death of judgment debtor leave of court extension of lien Except where otherwise prescribed by law, after the death of a judgment debtor, an execution upon a money judgment shall not be levied upon any debt owed to him or any property in which he has an interest, nor shall any other enforcement procedure be undertaken with respect to such debt or property, except upon leave of the surrogate’s court which granted letters testamentary or letters of administration upon the estate.

atoms.instrument: NY CPLR
atoms.condition: The landlord settles a former tenant's action over the deposit.
atoms.effect: It pays within twenty-one days after the tenant tenders a signed release and stipulation of discontinuance, or the tenant may enter judgment for the settlement amount with interest, costs and fees.
atoms.quote: Civil Practice Law & Rules Section 5003-A Prompt payment following settlement (a) When an action to recover damages has been settled, any settling defendant, except those defendants to whom subdivisions (b) and (c) of this section apply, shall pay all sums due to any settling plaintiff within twenty-one days of tender, by the settling plaintiff to the settling defendant, of a duly executed release and a stipulation discontinuing action executed on behalf of the settling plaintiff.

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law
atoms.condition: Mailing a statement or collection letter to a former tenant; or a former tenant claims identity theft.
atoms.effect: The tenant's social security number is not printed on anything mailed to the tenant unless law requires it. The identity-theft cease-collection procedure of 604-a is part of art. 29-H and governs principal creditors of consumer claims, so it does not govern a lease balance (NY:ADJ-lease-balance-not-consumer-credit); a claim that someone else incurred the balance is handled as a dispute under the federal and city rules.
atoms.reasoning: Section 604-a sits in article 29-H, whose 'principal creditor' and 'consumer claim' definitions require credit; a lease balance is not one.
atoms.quote: (e) Print an individual’s social security account number on any materials that are mailed to the individual, unless state or federal law requires the social security account number to be on the document to be mailed.

construction.quote: 1. Upon receipt from a debtor of the following, a principal creditor shall cease collection activities until completion of the review provided in subdivision five of this section

atoms.instrument: NY Abandoned Property Law
atoms.condition: An unclaimed refund is due to be reported.
