atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:Partnership Law 121-1502 (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Partnership Law art. 8-A (Revised Limited Partnership Act)
atoms.actor: owner (domestic or foreign limited partnership) or a collector suing in its name
atoms.condition: The party whose address the owner limited partnership designated for service of process filed a certificate of resignation, and the partnership has not filed a certificate designating a new address, when it or a collector in its name sues a former tenant.
atoms.effect: The partnership's authority to do business in New York is suspended, so it cannot maintain the suit until it files the certificate designating a new address, which ends the suspension; process against it may meanwhile be served on the Secretary of State. The lease and deposit statement are unaffected.
atoms.quote: Upon the failure of the designating limited partnership to file a certificate of amendment or change providing for the designation by the limited partnership of the new address after the filing of a certificate of resignation for receipt of process with the secretary of state, its authority to do business in this state shall be suspended.

construction.quote: Failure to comply with these requirements precludes a limited liability company from maintaining any action or special proceeding in New York

atoms.reasoning: Suspension of authority to do business bars maintaining an action as with the publication suspensions (NY:LLC-206-publication-suspension); the section itself provides for service on the Secretary of State while suspended.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:Partnership Law 121-104-A (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Partnership Law art. 8-A (Revised Limited Partnership Act)
atoms.condition: The owner limited partnership merges or consolidates into another limited partnership before the departing tenant's account is closed.
atoms.effect: The building, the deposit held in trust and the claim for the balance vest in the surviving or resulting partnership, which is liable for the refund, the statement and every deposit obligation as if it had incurred them; statements and suits proceed in its name, and a pending suit by or against the old partnership continues against or by the survivor.
atoms.quote: the surviving or resulting limited partnership shall be liable for all debts, obligations, liabilities and penalties of each constituent limited partnership as though each such debt, obligation, liability or penalty had been originally incurred by such surviving or resulting limited partnership
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:Partnership Law 121-1104 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.actor: landlord or manager keeping a hotel, boarding house or rooming house in New York City
atoms.condition: The landlord keeps a hotel, boarding house or rooming house in one of the counties of New York City, and a roomer or boarder who is not a member of the keeper's family dies there.
atoms.effect: Within 12 hours of the death the keeper reports in writing to the public administrator of the county the information it has about the deceased. The refund, belongings and any balance then follow the tenant-death rules (NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee, NY:SCPA-1112-public-administrator).
atoms.quote: Every person keeping a hotel, boarding or rooming house in any of the counties to which this article applies shall report in writing to the public administrator of his county information concerning every person not a member of his family who shall die in his hotel or house within 12 hours after such death.

construction.quote: The office of public administrator within the counties of the city of New York hereby is continued.

atoms.reasoning: Article 11 of the SCPA governs the public administrators of the counties of New York City.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1113 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: A former tenant died in New York City with gross assets within the small-estate amount of SCPA 1301 ($50,000), and the county public administrator acts on the estate without letters.
atoms.effect: The public administrator has all the powers of a fiduciary. Paying the refund (or delivering belongings) to it against its certificate of authority and receipt is a complete release and discharge, with the same effect as payment to any other fiduciary; the landlord need not see to how it is applied. The landlord's claim for a balance is presented to the public administrator.
atoms.quote: shall constitute a complete release and discharge for any payment of money or delivery of property made pursuant to the certificate without such person being required to see to the application thereof and with the same effect as if made to any other fiduciary.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1115 (partial, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: Branch (a): a former tenant died leaving a refund or belongings in the county, and no one is eligible to act as fiduciary, or the named executor refuses or neglects to act, is dead, missing or ineligible. Branch (b): an individual owner died intestate with unknown distributees or distributees domiciled outside New York, or testate with a named executor who does not act, is dead, missing or ineligible.
atoms.effect: (a) Before letters, the public administrator may take possession of and collect the tenant's personal property in the county: the refund is paid to it and belongings released to it. (b) Before letters, the public administrator may take possession of the building, manage it and collect its rents, so rent and the departing tenant's balance are collected for it and the manager takes direction from it (NY:COMMONLAW-owner-death-agency).
atoms.quote: Take possession of, manage and collect the rents of the real property of an intestate whose distributees are unknown or, whose distributees if known, are non-domiciliaries
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1118 (partial, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: At a tenant's death the landlord's claim is contingent or unliquidated (for example rent that will accrue until the estate terminates the lease under NY:RPL-236-a, or damage whose repair cost has not been fixed).
atoms.effect: The landlord may file with the fiduciary an affidavit showing the facts of the liability and its probable amount; the estate may then make no distribution without reserving assets the court finds adequate to pay the claim when it becomes due. When the claim becomes fixed before the final accounting, the landlord files the fixed claim under SCPA 1803 (NY:SCPA-1803-claim-form); otherwise the final decree keeps assets back to pay it when fixed.
atoms.quote: a claimant or a surety shall have the right to file with the fiduciary an affidavit showing the facts upon which the contingent or unliquidated liability is based and the probable amount thereof
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1804 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: The landlord presented its claim for a deceased former tenant's balance to the fiduciary under SCPA 1803.
atoms.effect: The fiduciary must promptly notify the landlord in writing of allowance or rejection, giving reasons for any rejection. If the fiduciary has not allowed the claim within 90 days after presentation, it is deemed rejected on the 90th day, and the 60-day period to sue runs from then (NY:SCPA-1810-sue-within-60-days). An allowed claim establishes its validity, and the landlord may petition the court to direct the fiduciary to pay it.
atoms.quote: If the fiduciary shall fail to allow the claim within 90 days from the date that it has been presented to him, the claim shall be deemed to have been rejected.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1806 (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: The landlord presents a claim for a deceased former tenant's balance under SCPA 1803, and the fiduciary rejects it in whole or part (or it is deemed rejected).
atoms.effect: For every limitation period, presenting the claim as SCPA 1803 requires counts as instituting a special proceeding to collect it, so a claim presented before the lease-claim period expires (NY:CPLR-213(2), extended by NY:CPLR-210-death) is timely. If the landlord does not sue within 60 days of rejection (NY:SCPA-1810-sue-within-60-days), the claim's validity is tried on the fiduciary's judicial accounting, where the landlord may file objections within 8 days of the return of process.
atoms.quote: the presentation of a claim as provided in 1803 shall be deemed the institution of a special proceeding for the collection of the claim.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1808 (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: The fiduciary of a deceased former tenant rejected the landlord's presented claim in whole or part, or it was deemed rejected after 90 days (NY:SCPA-1806-allowance-rejection), and the landlord wants to sue in a court of law or equity rather than have the claim tried on the accounting.
atoms.effect: The action must be commenced within 60 days after the rejection or deemed rejection. Missing the 60 days does not lose the claim: it is then determined on the judicial settlement of the fiduciary's account (NY:SCPA-1808-presentation-tolls), and the landlord keeps any right to a jury trial.
atoms.quote: where a claim has been presented and rejected or deemed rejected pursuant to 1806 in whole or in part the action must be commenced within 60 days after such rejection.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1810 (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: The executor or administrator of a deceased tenant (or owner) presents limited or restricted letters.
atoms.effect: The fiduciary may act only within the limits stated in the letters: letters limited to prosecuting or defending a claim, or restraining compromise or enforcement of a judgment, or confining it to specified property, do not authorize receiving the refund or settling the balance beyond those limits. Pay or settle only within the letters' terms; otherwise with a fiduciary holding full letters or the court's further order.
atoms.quote: Letters may be granted limiting and restricting the powers and rights of the holder thereof:
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 702 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: A person claims to be the executor or administrator of a deceased tenant or owner.
atoms.effect: Letters are conclusive evidence of the holder's authority until reversed or modified on appeal, or suspended, modified or revoked by the issuing court. A clerk's certificate of letters is sufficient evidence of the letters and the fiduciary's identity for six months after it issues; after six months ask for a current certificate before paying. Paying the refund to the holder of letters shown this way discharges the landlord (NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee).
atoms.quote: A certificate of letters testamentary or of administration duly issued by the clerk of the court shall be sufficient evidence, subject to the provisions of subdivision one hereof, of the existence of such letters and the identity of the fiduciary for all purposes for six months after the date of such issuance.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 703 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: One of several fiduciaries of a deceased tenant or owner dies, is removed or has its letters revoked; or all of them do.
atoms.effect: (a) With one or more remaining, no successor is appointed (unless the will requires one); the remaining fiduciaries complete the administration and continue pending suits, so they receive the refund and settle the balance. (b) If none remains, the court appoints a successor, who completes the administration, continues pending suits in its own name and enforces judgments for the estate; deal with the successor, not with the representative of a deceased fiduciary (NY:EPTL-11-3.4-no-representative-of-representative).
atoms.quote: the others may proceed and complete the administration of the estate pursuant to the letters or lifetime trust instrument and may continue any action or special proceeding brought by or against all.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 706 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: A voluntary administrator (small estate, short certificate) acts for a deceased individual owner or a deceased tenant.
atoms.effect: It has no authority over the deceased's interest in New York real property. For a deceased owner it may collect rent that had accrued before death (personal property, NY:EPTL-13-1.1-accrued-rent-leasehold) but may not manage the building, collect later rents or direct the manager as to it; that authority lies with the fiduciary on letters or the persons to whom the building passed. For a deceased tenant, the refund and the lease claim are personal property within its authority.
atoms.quote: This article is not applicable to any interest in real property in this state owned by a decedent, but his owner ship of an interest in real property shall not prevent the use of this article in administering his personal property.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1302 (partial, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: A former tenant died domiciled in another state, and a person presents a certified copy of that state's small-estate affidavit or short certificate to collect the refund.
atoms.effect: The landlord may recognize it and pay the refund to that person, provided the other state recognizes and pays on New York short certificates. Without that reciprocity, pay only a New York voluntary administrator, a fiduciary on letters (NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee) or a foreign fiduciary under NY:EPTL-13-3.4-foreign-fiduciary. Using the small-estate route is optional for the estate.
atoms.quote: may recognize a certified copy of an affidavit or of a short certificate of a judge or clerk of a probate court made under a statute of another state, providing for the settlement of small estates without administration
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1309 (partial, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: A former tenant died intestate owing a balance (or leaving property the landlord must account for), and no one has sought letters.
atoms.effect: The landlord, as a creditor, may petition the surrogate's court for letters of administration to be granted to another person or to itself. Where no distributee takes letters and no one is appointed by consent, letters go to the public administrator (or county chief fiscal officer), or in the court's discretion to the petitioner. The claim is then presented to the administrator (NY:SCPA-1803-claim-form).
atoms.quote: creditor or a person interested in an action brought or about to be brought in which the intestate or the person alleged to be deceased, if living, would be a proper party may present a petition to the court having jurisdiction praying for a decree granting letters of administration to him or to another person

construction.quote: to the petitioner, in the discretion of the court, or

atoms.reasoning: 1002 lets a creditor petition; 1001(8) sets the fallback order when no distributee takes letters.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 1002 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: The landlord paid the refund to, or settled the balance with, a tenant's (or owner's) executor or administrator whose letters were later suspended, modified or revoked, or who was removed.
atoms.effect: The payment or settlement stays valid if it was within the fiduciary's powers and the landlord acted in good faith before the removal, suspension, modification or revocation, or before process in the removal proceeding was served (or after service where the fiduciary's powers over that act were not suspended). After the decree the former fiduciary's powers cease: pay or settle only with the successor or the person the decree names.
atoms.quote: does not affect the validity of any act within the powers of the fiduciary done by him before his removal or the suspension, modification or revocation of his letters or the service of process, where the other party acted in good faith
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 720 (partial, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Surrogate's Court Procedure Act
atoms.condition: Two different surrogate's courts have issued letters on the same deceased tenant's or owner's estate.
atoms.effect: The person to whom letters were first issued, on a good-faith application, has exclusive authority and is the payee. Acts of the later holder done in good faith before notice of the first letters (for example receiving the refund) remain valid; once the landlord has notice of the first letters, it deals only with their holder.
atoms.quote: But the acts of a person to whom letters were afterwards issued, done in good faith before notice of the letters first issued are valid
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SCPA 704 (new_rule, minor)

atoms.instrument: NY Estates, Powers and Trusts Law
atoms.condition: Branch (a): an estate owns the building and its executor or administrator runs it (so the deposit refund and statement duties arise during administration). Branch (b): a deceased tenant's executor or administrator kept or used the unit, or entered a settlement or payment plan with the landlord, during administration.
atoms.effect: Claims on contracts the fiduciary made in its fiduciary capacity, on obligations from the estate's ownership or control of property (for example the deposit refund owed by an estate-owned building, or use and occupancy owed by the estate), or on torts in administration are asserted against the estate by suing the fiduciary in its fiduciary capacity. The fiduciary is personally liable on such a contract only if it did not disclose its representative capacity and identify the estate, and personally liable for ownership obligations or torts only if it failed to exercise reasonable care, diligence and prudence.
judgment_terms: failed to exercise reasonable care, diligence and prudence
atoms.quote: Claims based on contracts entered into by a personal representative in his fiduciary capacity, on obligations arising from ownership or control of the estate or on torts committed in the course of estate administration may be asserted against the estate by proceeding against the personal representative in his fiduciary capacity
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:EPTL 11-4.7 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Executive Law art. 15 (Human Rights Law)
atoms.actor: landlord, managing agent, Handoff or collector offering deferred payment
atoms.condition: A former tenant owes a balance and asks for, or is offered, time to pay it (a payment plan, installment agreement or deferral), which is credit: a right conferred by a creditor to incur debt and defer its payment, with or without a finance charge.
atoms.effect: Whoever grants the plan is a creditor for this purpose. It may not grant, withhold, extend or set the terms of the plan (length, down payment, interest, co-signer) differently because of race, creed, color, national origin, citizenship or immigration status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, military status, age, sex, marital status, domestic-violence victim status, disability or familial status, nor ask about childbearing or birth control, nor refuse to consider, or discount, a source of the tenant's income for those reasons. Differences based on factually supportable, objective differences in overall creditworthiness (current income, assets, prior credit history) are lawful. On the tenant's request, a creditor that rejects a plan request gives the specific reasons. Remedies follow NY:EXC-297(9)-remedies.
judgment_terms: factually supportable, objective differences in overall credit worthiness
atoms.quote: To discriminate in the granting, withholding, extending or renewing, or in the fixing of the rates, terms or conditions of, any form of credit

construction.quote: The term “credit”, when used in this article means the right conferred upon a person by a creditor to incur debt and defer its payment, whether or not any interest or finance charge is made for the exercise of this right.

atoms.reasoning: A payment plan confers a right to defer payment of the balance, which is credit under 292, and the landlord granting it extends credit and so is a creditor.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:Executive Law 296-A (partial, major)

atoms.instrument: NY General Business Law art. 25 (Fair Credit Reporting Act)
atoms.actor: landlord, its managing agent or Handoff as agent, a collector, or an assignee of the balance
atoms.condition: The former tenant has placed a security freeze on its consumer credit report, and the landlord (or its subsidiary, affiliate or agent, or an assignee or prospective buyer of the balance) wants the report.
atoms.effect: The freeze does not apply to the use of the report by a person with which the tenant had a contract (the lease), or its agent or assignee, for reviewing the account or collecting the obligation owed under that contract; for that purpose the report may still be obtained. For any other purpose the freeze applies and the agency may not release it. The purpose limits of NY:GBL-380-b-permissible-purpose still apply.
atoms.quote: with which the consumer has or had prior to assignment an account or contract, including a demand deposit account, or to whom the consumer issued a negotiable instrument, for the purposes of reviewing the account or collecting the financial obligation owing for the account, contract, or negotiable instrument.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:GBL 380-T (new_rule, minor)

atoms.instrument: NY Uniform Commercial Code art. 3 (commercial paper)
atoms.actor: landlord or managing agent paying a refund by check
atoms.condition: The refund is owed to two or more co-tenants and is paid by one check naming more than one payee.
atoms.effect: A check payable to the payees in the alternative ("A or B") may be negotiated, discharged or enforced by any one payee who holds it; a check payable to them jointly ("A and B") may be negotiated, discharged or enforced only by all of them together. So: where the refund is joint and paying the whole to any one discharges the landlord (NY:ADJ-cotenants-payee branch (a)), either form discharges it once paid; where records show each co-tenant's share (branch (b)), a check payable "A or B" lets one co-tenant take the whole and does not discharge the landlord as to the others, so pay separate checks in the proportions owed or one check payable jointly ("A and B").
atoms.quote: if not in the alternative is payable to all of them and may be negotiated, discharged or enforced only by all of them.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:UCC 3-116 (partial, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Uniform Commercial Code art. 3 (commercial paper)
atoms.actor: managing agent, Handoff or their staff signing refund checks for the owner
atoms.condition: A managing agent, Handoff or an employee signs a refund check (or other instrument) drawn for the owner.
atoms.effect: Configuration (a): the check names the owner and the signature shows representative capacity (for example "Owner LLC, by Jane Doe, Agent", or the organization's name with the signer's name and office): the signer is not personally liable on it. (b) The check neither names the owner nor shows representative capacity: the signer is personally liable on it to any holder. (c) It names the owner but does not show capacity, or shows capacity but does not name the owner: the signer is personally liable, except as against the immediate party (the tenant) where it is shown that both understood the signer acted for the owner. Checks drawn on the owner's or the manager's escrow account in the owner's name with a representative signature fall in (a).
atoms.quote: is personally obligated if the instrument neither names the person represented nor shows that the representative signed in a representative capacity
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:UCC 3-403 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Uniform Commercial Code art. 3 (commercial paper)
atoms.condition: Branch (a): the landlord pays the refund by its own (or its manager's) check. Branch (b): the landlord pays the refund by a bank's cashier's or teller's check with no recourse against it. Branch (c): the former tenant pays the balance by personal check.
atoms.effect: (a) The refund obligation is suspended from delivery until the check is presented; if the check is dishonored (for example for insufficient funds or a stop-payment order), the tenant may sue on the check or on the deposit claim. The deposit is returned only when the check is paid: a dishonored refund check not replaced by payment within the 14 days means the refund was not returned on time (NY:GOL-7-108(1-a)(e)-forfeiture). (b) The refund obligation is discharged to the check's amount when the tenant takes it. (c) The balance is suspended until presentment; if the tenant's check is dishonored, the landlord may sue on the check or on the balance (returned-check fee limits: NY:RPL-238-a(2-a)); payment of the check discharges the balance to its amount. A check marked "payment in full" is governed by NY:UCC-1-308-full-payment-check.
atoms.quote: in any other case the obligation is suspended pro tanto until the instrument is due or if it is payable on demand until its presentment. If the instrument is dishonored action may be maintained on either the instrument or the obligation
atoms.reasoning: A drawer's own check only suspends the refund obligation; on dishonor the obligation is enforceable as if unpaid, so the deposit was not returned by the dishonored check. A bank-drawn check without recourse discharges it.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:UCC 3-802 (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Uniform Commercial Code art. 3 (commercial paper)
atoms.condition: The former tenant says the refund check was lost, destroyed or stolen before it was paid.
atoms.effect: The refund is not paid by a check that was never paid (NY:UCC-3-802-check-suspends-obligation), and the tenant, as owner of the lost check, may sue and recover from the landlord on proof of ownership, the facts preventing its production and its terms; the court must then require security of at least twice the unpaid amount indemnifying the landlord against later claims on the check. Reissuing a replacement check or electronic payment satisfies the refund; the landlord's exposure to a later holder of the original check is what the security protects.
atoms.quote: The court shall require security, in an amount fixed by the court not less than twice the amount allegedly unpaid on the instrument, indemnifying the defendant
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:UCC 3-804 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: 18 NYCRR Part 352 (public assistance)
atoms.actor: landlord participating in a district homeless-family housing allowance program
atoms.condition: The landlord received an allowance from the social services district to secure an apartment for a homeless family under 18 NYCRR 352.3(i), agreeing to keep a specified apartment available to the family for a set period (up to 32 months), and the family leaves before that period ends, for any reason.
atoms.effect: The landlord must return to the district a pro rata portion of the allowance reflecting the balance of the period not used. This is owed to the district, not the tenant, and is not a deduction from the tenant's deposit; the district may place another eligible family in the apartment for the balance of the period. The tenant's own deposit and account are settled separately under the ordinary rules.
atoms.quote: the landlord will return a pro rata portion of the allowance reflecting the balance of the period.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:18 NYCRR 352.3 (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Social Services Law
atoms.condition: The landlord or its agent seeks or obtains payment from a social services district for housing furnished to a public-assistance household: a claim on a security voucher or agreement (NYC:HRA-voucher-claim-window), a claim under a housing allowance, or direct shelter payments; and the claim or a statement supporting it is knowingly false or conceals a material fact (for example damage the tenant did not cause, rent for months after the household left, or failure to disclose payments already received).
atoms.effect: The district or the State may recover civil damages of three times the amount falsely overstated (or three times its damages for a non-monetary falsehood), or $5,000, whichever is greater. A claim for payment made to a political subdivision or its contractor is a statement for this purpose, and any payment funded in part by public money counts. Claims on vouchers therefore carry only the itemized, supported amounts the ordinary deposit rules would allow (NY:GOL-7-108(1-a)(b)-refundable, NYC:HRA-voucher-proof).
judgment_terms: deliberate concealment of any material fact
atoms.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation knowingly by means of a false statement or representation, or by deliberate concealment of any material fact, or other fraudulent scheme or device, on behalf of himself or others, to attempt to obtain or to obtain payment from public funds for services or supplies furnished or purportedly furnished pursuant to this chapter.

construction.quote: three times the amount by which any figure is falsely overstated

atoms.reasoning: Housing furnished to a recipient under a security agreement (SSL 143-c) or shelter allowance (SSL 131-a) is furnished pursuant to the Social Services Law, and a claim for payment made to a social services district is a statement under 145-b(1)(b).
atoms.origin: register queue batch 4, section NY:SSL 145-B (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: 19 NYCRR (Department of State)
atoms.condition: Configuration 3 applies: individuals (for example Handoff's people) collect or attempt to collect a rent balance as real estate salespersons associated with a licensed broker (for example the manager's brokerage).
atoms.effect: The broker supervises each such salesperson by regular, frequent and consistent personal guidance, instruction, oversight and superintendence of the brokerage business the salesperson conducts, including the collection work; a broker whose name the salespersons use without that supervision does not meet the association RPL 441(1)(d) requires, and the broker's licence is exposed under NY:RPL-441-c-licence-discipline. The broker and the salesperson each keep written records of every transaction the salesperson effects or assists with, sufficient to identify it and showing its dates.
atoms.quote: (a) The supervision of a real estate salesman by a licensed real estate broker, required by subdivision 1(d) of section 441 of the Real Property Law, shall consist of regular, frequent and consistent personal guidance, instruction, oversight and superintendence by the real estate broker with respect to the general real estate brokerage business conducted by the broker, and all matters relating thereto.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 7, section NY:19 NYCRR 175.21 (partial, major)

atoms.instrument: New York Business Corporation Law
atoms.actor: owner (foreign corporation); collector in its name
atoms.condition: The owner is a corporation formed outside New York, and it or a collector in its name is about to sue a former tenant or settle the tenancy account.
atoms.effect: Only activity other than the acts listed in 1301(b) counts toward 'doing business' for the BCL 1312 bar: maintaining or defending an action or proceeding, settling it or settling claims or disputes (including the tenant's deposit claim or the balance), holding directors' or shareholders' meetings, keeping bank accounts (including the deposit account), and securities-transfer offices are not doing business. Owning and leasing New York units is weighed under NY:BCL-1312(a)-foreign-authority; a corporation whose only New York acts are those listed may sue without authority. A foreign corporation authorized under a fictitious name because its own name was unavailable must use that fictitious name in its New York business, including leases, statements and suits, and GBL 130 does not apply to that name: no assumed-name certificate is needed before suing on a lease made in it, and a GBL 130 filing does not adopt a fictitious name. A lease made in any other name than the corporate or filed fictitious name stays subject to NY:GBL-130-assumed-name.
atoms.quote: (b) Without excluding other activities which may not constitute doing business in this state, a foreign corporation shall not be considered to be doing business in this state, for the purposes of this chapter, by reason of carrying on in this state any one or more of the following activities: (1) Maintaining or defending any action or proceeding, whether judicial, administrative, arbitrative or otherwise, or effecting settlement thereof or the settlement of claims or disputes.

construction.quote: The provisions of section one hundred thirty of the general business law shall not apply to any fictitious name filed by a foreign corporation pursuant to this section

atoms.reasoning: 1301(d) excludes GBL 130 for a filed fictitious name, so the assumed-name precondition does not reach it.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 7, section NY:BCL 1301 (partial, major)

atoms.instrument: New York Business Corporation Law
atoms.actor: owner (foreign corporation); collector in its name
atoms.condition: An authorized foreign corporation owning the unit changed its corporate name or its jurisdiction of incorporation in its home jurisdiction and did not deliver a certificate of amendment to the Department of State within 20 days after the change took effect there.
atoms.effect: From the 21st day its New York authority is suspended, so while suspended it is not authorized and cannot maintain a suit against a former tenant (NY:BCL-1312(a)-foreign-authority). If the Department of State files the amendment within 120 days after the change, the suspension is annulled and authority continues as if never suspended. The Secretary of State remains its agent for process on liabilities incurred before the filing, so the tenant's suit on the deposit is served there. Operator step: before suing, confirm the owner's New York authority is not suspended and the name on the suit matches the name on file.
atoms.quote: If an authorized foreign corporation has changed its name in the jurisdiction of its incorporation, or has changed its jurisdiction of incorporation, it shall deliver to the department of state within twenty days after the change became effective in that jurisdiction a certificate of amendment under paragraph (a) of this section. Upon its failure to deliver such certificate, its authority to do business in this state shall upon the expiration of said twenty days be suspended.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 7, section NY:BCL 1309 (partial, minor)

atoms.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
atoms.actor: landlord (plaintiff); collector suing in its name
atoms.condition: The landlord or its collector sues a former tenant in the NYC Civil Court for a residential lease balance (rent, use and occupancy, damage or other lease charges), and the action is commenced before NY:S9760-venue takes effect.
atoms.effect: The action does not arise out of a 'consumer credit transaction' as CCA 2101(g) defines it (credit extended to an individual), so the tenant-county rule of CCA 301(a) for consumer credit actions does not apply. The action is brought in the county within the city where one of the parties resides when it is commenced: the tenant's county, or the owner's county, an entity owner residing in any county where it transacts business or keeps an office (CCA 305). If the plaintiff is an assignee of the claim (a collector or buyer suing in its own name), the original owner is treated as the plaintiff for venue. If no party resides in the city, CCA 301(b) governs. For actions commenced on or after the day NY:S9760-venue applies, that rule controls instead and the action lies only where the tenant resides or the transaction took place. The added consumer-credit filing fee does not apply (NY:CCA-1911-clerk-fees).
atoms.quote: (g) "Consumer credit transaction" means a transaction wherein credit is extended to an individual

construction.quote: (a) in an action arising out of a consumer credit transaction where a purchaser, borrower, or a debtor is a defendant, if a defendant resides in the city of New York, or if such transaction took place therein, in the county in which a defendant resides at the commencement thereof or in the county in which such transaction took place, and in all other cases, in the county in which one of the parties resides at the commencement thereof; or

(a) If the plaintiff is an assignee of the cause of action, the original owner of the cause of action shall be deemed the plaintiff for the purpose of determining proper venue. (b) A corporation, joint-stock association or other unincorporated association shall be deemed a resident of any county wherein it transacts business, keeps an office, has an agency or is established by law.

atoms.reasoning: CCA 301(a) confines the defendant's-county rule to 'an action arising out of a consumer credit transaction' and sends 'all other cases' to the county where one of the parties resides; the lease balance is not a credit extension (NY:ADJ-lease-balance-not-consumer-credit), so it is in 'all other cases'. Venue is one rule set in time: this rule today, NY:S9760-venue from its effective date. CCA 305 (merged here) fixes where an entity resides and treats an assignee's assignor as the plaintiff.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 7, section NY:CCA 2101 (partial, major); merged: NY:CCA-305-venue-residence

atoms.instrument: New York Civil Practice Law and Rules
atoms.actor: landlord and its attorney; tenant's representative
atoms.condition: The landlord settles a claim with a former tenant who is an infant, adjudicated incompetent or conservatee (the tenant's deposit claim or the landlord's balance claim), so the settlement needs court approval under CPLR 1207.
atoms.effect: The application includes an affidavit of the tenant's representative stating his name, residence and relationship; the tenant's name, age and residence; the circumstances of the claim; the nature and extent of the damages; the settlement terms and proposed distribution and his approval of both; any other settlement application on the same claim; any reimbursement received; and any related family claim. If the tenant or representative has an attorney, that attorney's affidavit states the reasons for recommending the settlement, that he is not concerned in it at the landlord's instance and takes no compensation from the landlord, and his services. At the hearing the moving party, the tenant and his attorney attend unless excused for good cause. No attorney with an interest conflicting with the tenant's may represent him, so the landlord's attorney never represents the tenant; if the tenant has no attorney, the landlord's attorney may prepare the papers and they must say so. A settlement without this approval does not bind (dependency).
atoms.quote: (e) Representation. No attorney having or representing any interest conflicting with that of an infant or incompetent may represent the infant or incompetent. (f) Preparation of papers by attorney for adverse party. If the infant or incompetent is not represented by an attorney the papers may be prepared by the attorney for an adverse party or person and shall state that fact.

atoms.condition: A landlord, manager, Handoff or collector prepares or sends business stationery in the settlement chain: the itemized statement, a refund check, a balance or demand letter, an invoice, or their envelopes.

atoms.instrument: New York Limited Liability Company Law
atoms.actor: owner (foreign LLC); collector in its name
atoms.condition: The owner is a limited liability company formed outside New York, and it or a collector in its name is about to sue a former tenant or settle the tenancy account.
atoms.effect: Only activity other than the acts listed in 803(a) counts toward 'doing business' for the LLC Law 808 bar: maintaining or defending an action or proceeding, settling it or settling claims or disputes (including the tenant's deposit claim or the balance), holding members' or managers' meetings, keeping bank accounts (including the deposit account), and offices only for membership-interest transfers are not doing business. Owning and regularly leasing New York units is weighed under NY:LLC-808(a)-foreign-authority; a foreign LLC whose only New York acts are those listed may sue without a certificate of authority. The list does not decide whether the LLC may be served with process in New York.
atoms.quote: (a) Without excluding other activities that may not constitute doing business in this state, a foreign limited liability company shall not be considered to be doing business in this state for the purposes of this chapter, by reason of carrying on in this state any one or more of the following activities: (1) maintaining or defending any action or proceeding, whether judicial, administrative, arbitrative or otherwise or effecting settlement thereof or the settlement of claims or disputes;
atoms.origin: register queue batch 7, section NY:LLC Law 803 (partial, major)

atoms.instrument: New York Not-for-Profit Corporation Law
atoms.actor: owner (foreign not-for-profit corporation); collector suing in its name
atoms.condition: The owner is a foreign not-for-profit corporation authorized to conduct activities in New York that changed its name in its state of incorporation and did not deliver a certificate of amendment of its application for authority to the Department of State within twenty days after the change took effect; it (or a collector in its name) sues or would sue a former tenant for a balance.
atoms.effect: From the twenty-first day after the name change its New York authority is suspended, so it is a foreign corporation conducting activities without authority and cannot maintain the suit (NY:NPCL-1313-foreign-authority). Branch (a): the Department of State files a certificate of amendment changing the name within 120 days after the name change took effect: the suspension is annulled and authority continues as if no suspension had occurred, so capacity to sue is restored for the whole period. Branch (b): no such filing within 120 days: the suspension stands and the corporation cannot maintain the suit until it is authorized and has paid the fees, penalties and franchise taxes 1313(a) requires. In both branches the lease, the deposit statement, the tenant's right to sue it and its defense of the tenant's suit are unaffected (1313(b)), and the Secretary of State remains its agent for the tenant's process during the suspension. Check the Department of State entity record for a name change before a suit is filed.
atoms.quote: If an authorized foreign corporation has changed its name in the jurisdiction of its incorporation, it shall deliver to the department of state within twenty days after the change became effective in that jurisdiction a certificate of amendment under paragraph (a). Upon its failure to deliver such certificate, its authority to conduct activities in this state shall upon the expiration of said twenty days be suspended. The filing by the department of state of a certificate of amendment changing the corporation name within one hundred twenty days after the effective date of the change of name in the jurisdiction of its incorporation shall annul the suspension and its authority to conduct activities in this state shall be restored and continue as if no suspension had occurred.

construction.quote: A foreign corporation conducting activities in this state without authority shall not maintain any action or special proceeding in this state unless and until such corporation has been authorized

atoms.reasoning: 1309(b) suspends the authority of a foreign not-for-profit that fails to file its name change within twenty days; a corporation whose authority is suspended conducts activities without authority, which 1313(a) bars from maintaining any action until authorized (NY:NPCL-1313-foreign-authority). The 120-day filing annuls the suspension retroactively ('as if no suspension had occurred'); absent it, 1313(a)'s own cure (authorization plus back fees) governs.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 8, section NY:N-PCL 1309 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Partnership Law art. 8-B (limited liability partnerships)
atoms.actor: owner (foreign related limited liability partnership) or a collector suing in its name
atoms.condition: The owner is a foreign related limited liability partnership (a foreign LLP that obtained a certificate of authority under LLC Law 802) that leases NYC units, and it or a collector in its name sues a former tenant.
atoms.effect: Branch (a): within five years after it filed its application for the LLC Law 802 certificate of authority, having satisfied all of 802's requirements, it is deemed to have filed the 121-1502 notice, so the 121-1502 bar for a foreign LLP that has not filed its notice does not apply. Branch (b): from the fifth anniversary of that application it must file the 121-1502 notice; if it has not, it cannot maintain the suit until it files the notice and pays the fees (NY:PTR-121-1502-foreign-llp).
atoms.quote: Any foreign related limited liability partnership that has filed a certificate of authority under and satisfied all the requirements of section eight hundred two of the limited liability company law shall be deemed to have filed a notice pursuant to section 121-1502 of this chapter until the fifth anniversary of filing its application for such certificate of authority, at which time the foreign related limited liability partnership shall file a notice pursuant to section 121-1502 of this chapter.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 8, section NY:Partnership Law 121-1504 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Partnership Law art. 8-B (limited liability partnerships)
atoms.actor: owner (New York registered limited liability partnership) or a collector suing in its name
atoms.condition: The owner is a New York registered limited liability partnership; the party whose address it designated for the Secretary of State to mail process filed a certificate of resignation for receipt of process, and the partnership has not filed a certificate of amendment or statement designating a new address, when it or a collector in its name sues a former tenant.
atoms.effect: Its authority to do business in New York is suspended, so it cannot maintain the suit until the Department of State files its certificate of amendment or statement of a new address; that filing annuls the suspension and restores authority as if no suspension had occurred. While suspended, the tenant may serve process on the partnership through the Secretary of State. The lease and the deposit statement are unaffected.
atoms.quote: Upon the failure of the designating limited liability partnership to file a certificate of amendment providing for the designation by the limited liability partnership of the new address after the filing of a certificate of resignation for receipt of process with the secretary of state, its authority to do business in this state shall be suspended.

construction.quote: Failure to comply with these requirements precludes a limited liability company from maintaining any action or special proceeding in New York
shall annul the suspension and its authority to do business in this state shall be restored and continued as if no suspension had occurred.

atoms.reasoning: Suspension of authority to do business bars maintaining an action, as with the publication suspensions (NY:LLC-206-publication-suspension); 121-1506(d) annuls it retroactively on filing a new address. NY:PTR-121-104-a-process-address-suspension states the same rule for limited partnerships; this is the LLP branch.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 8, section NY:Partnership Law 121-1506 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Partnership Law art. 8-A (Revised Limited Partnership Act)
atoms.actor: owner (New York limited partnership) or a collector suing in its name
atoms.condition: The owner is a New York limited partnership and it, or a collector in its name, sues or would sue a former tenant for a balance. Branch (a): the partnership was formed on or after the effective date of 121-201(c)(i) and did not file proof of publication (certificate of publication with the newspapers' affidavits) with the Department of State within 120 days after its formation. Branch (b): it was formed before that date, did not comply with the earlier publication requirement (a partnership formed before 1999-01-01, or formed from 1999-01-01 on that filed at least one publisher's affidavit, is deemed to have complied), and did not file proof of publication within twelve months after that date. Branch (c): it complied, or is deemed to have complied, with the requirement that applied to it.
atoms.effect: (a) and (b): its authority to carry on, conduct or transact business in New York is suspended from the end of the 120-day (or twelve-month) period, and while suspended it cannot maintain the suit. Filing proof of publication in substantial compliance at any time annuls the suspension, so the suit may proceed once it is filed. The suspension does not impair the lease, the deposit statement, any right or remedy of the tenant, the tenant's right to sue the partnership, or the partnership's defense of the tenant's suit, and does not make any partner or agent liable for the partnership's obligations. (c): no bar. Operator step: confirm the Department of State record shows the publication filing before suing.
atoms.quote: If within one hundred twenty days after its formation, proof of such publication, consisting of the certificate of publication of the limited partnership with the affidavits of publication of the newspapers annexed thereto has not been filed with the department of state, the authority of such limited partnership to carry on, conduct or transact any business in this state shall be suspended, effective as of the expiration of such one hundred twenty day period.

construction.quote: Failure to comply with these requirements precludes a limited liability company from maintaining any action or special proceeding in New York
such suspension of such limited partnership’s authority to carry on, conduct or transact business shall be annulled.

atoms.reasoning: 121-201(c) uses the same suspension and annulment words as LLC Law 206, which the Appellate Division reads as barring the entity from maintaining an action while suspended (NY:LLC-206-publication-suspension, Small Step Day Care); the section's savings clause preserves contracts, the other party's rights and suits and the partnership's defense, and filing proof annuls the suspension. NY:PTR-121-902-foreign-lp-publication covers foreign limited partnerships and NY:PTR-121-1500-llp-publication and NY:PTR-121-1502-foreign-llp cover LLPs (121-1500, 121-1502); this is the domestic limited partnership branch.
atoms.origin: register queue batch 8, section NY:Partnership Law 121-201 (new_rule, critical)

atoms.instrument: NY Partnership Law art. 8-A (Revised Limited Partnership Act)
atoms.actor: persons winding up a dissolved owner limited partnership; managing agent; collector
atoms.condition: The owner is a New York limited partnership that is dissolved (121-801 or 121-802) before a departing tenant's account is closed.
atoms.effect: Dissolution does not end the settlement or the claim. The persons winding up act in the partnership's name: the general partners who did not wrongfully dissolve it, or if none the limited partners, or, where the Supreme Court winds up the affairs on a partner's application or after a judicial dissolution under 121-802 (to which the partners' own winding-up right does not extend), the receiver or liquidating trustee it appoints. They may send the statement and refund, settle, and prosecute or defend suits in the partnership's name, including a suit for the former tenant's balance; the manager and any collector take instructions and pay remittances only to them. The deposit stays the tenant's trust money (NY:GOL-7-103(1)-trust) and is returned or applied under the deposit rules, not distributed to partners.
atoms.quote: Upon dissolution of a limited partnership, the persons winding up the limited partnership’s affairs may, in the name of, and for and on behalf of, the limited partnership prosecute and defend suits, whether civil, criminal or administrative, settle and close the limited partnership’s business, dispose of and convey the limited partnership’s property, discharge the limited partnership’s liabilities
atoms.origin: register queue batch 8, section NY:Partnership Law 121-803 (new_rule, major)

atoms.instrument: NY Partnership Law art. 8-A (Revised Limited Partnership Act)
atoms.actor: persons winding up a dissolved owner limited partnership
atoms.condition: A dissolved owner limited partnership winds up while a former tenant's refund, interest or damages claim (for example 7-108(1-a)(g) damages) is unpaid or in dispute.
atoms.effect: The partnership's assets go first to creditors, the former tenant included, by payment or by an adequate reserve for the claim, before any distribution to partners on their interests or contributions.
atoms.quote: to creditors, including partners who are creditors, to the extent permitted by law, in satisfaction of liabilities of the limited partnership, whether by payment or by establishment of adequate reserves
atoms.origin: register queue batch 8, section NY:Partnership Law 121-804 (new_rule, minor)

C1 NYC rent-stabilized unit.note: 7-108 never applies to a stabilized unit (7-108(1)). Lease or renewal entered on or after 2025-11-15: amended 7-107 applies in full (14-day written statement sent to the tenant, forfeiture, willfulness standard). Entered before: former 7-107 (successor liability only), and 7-108(1-a) does not come in through RSC 2525.4(d) (NY:ADJ-RS-pre2025-7108-inapplicable; Karole rejected). The deposit is then returned at the end of the tenancy unless the landlord proves damage or applies it to sums due under the lease, with the burden on the landlord. Commingling, or no bank notice left unrebutted, forfeits the deposit (App Div). 7-103 trust and interest apply either way; the RSC layer is the NYC worker's.

C2 NYC rent-controlled unit.note: Not a 7-107 unit, so 7-108 applies, but 7-108(1-a) excludes rent-control units. There is no statutory 14-day rule, cap or forfeiture at state level. Deposit conditions come from NYC rent-control regulations (9 NYCRR 2205.5; NYC worker) plus 7-103.

C3 NYC market-rate unit, building of 6+.note: The remainder returned within 14 days includes the interest balance less the 1% fee. Fees on the ledger are not retained (NY:ADJ-no-fee-retention). A month-to-month tenant may leave at the end of any month without notice unless an agreement requires notice. NYC Admin Code items belong to the NYC worker. Sweep 2026-09-29: utility payments the tenant made for the landlord are credited against rent (RPL 235-a); no rent after a constructive eviction and abandonment or after a vacate order the owner is responsible for; rent under a 7-A judgment or foreclosure receivership is collected by the administrator or receiver; Handoff settling statements without collecting rent needs no broker licence.

C4 NYC unit in a building of fewer than.note: Same as C3 except 7-103(2-a) does not require an interest-bearing account; units are counted per building, and other buildings of the same owner are not added (NY:ADJ-7103-2a-building-count). If the landlord used an interest-bearing account anyway, 7-103(2) interest (less 1%) is owed. If the deposit was banked, the bank-notice duty applies. 7-108(1-a) has no building-size threshold after 2019. A three-family house is a multiple dwelling: if it was converted after 1929-04-18 and has no certificate of occupancy for three families, no rent is recoverable for that period; if the owner is unregistered, rent is suspended until it registers and then recovered in full. Sweep 2026-09-29: a one- or two-family house with an illegal unit (two families at most) has no statutory rent bar; a third family makes it a multiple dwelling (MDL 302). An agreement that states a monthly rent and nothing about length is presumed month to month from the start (Gerolemou); RPL 232 runs to the first October 1 only where the parties contemplated a longer stay without fixing it; an agreement with its own notice terms governs; an oral term over one year is void and the tenancy is monthly. If the individual owner dies, the manager's collection authority ends.

C5a Lease signed before HSTPA (before 20.note: If the lease was renewed, continued month to month, or rent was accepted after it expired, on or after 2019-07-14, 7-108(1-a) applies (Case v 575 Classon; Bogom-Shanon). Otherwise 7-108(1-a) does not apply: old 7-108(1) scope (written leases in 6+ unit buildings, rent-controlled units) for successor liability, and the common-law return rule for the deposit. 227-e applies if the action is commenced after 2019-06-14. For stabilized units, see C1 and the 2025-11-15 date instead.

C6 Early termination.note: Rent after vacating is limited by the mitigation duty (the landlord bears the burden) or ended by a statutory termination right. A NYC month-to-month tenant may surrender at the end of any month without notice unless an agreement requires notice. The deposit clock still runs from vacating. An automatic-renewal clause binds only with the GOL 5-905 notice. In a unit covered by Good Cause Eviction, a landlord non-renewal does not end the tenancy (NY:RPL-215). At day 14 the deposit covers only rent already due and unpaid, up to a new lease. A lease-break sum is owed only if it is valid liquidated damages and is never kept from the deposit. Sweep 2026-09-29: a tenant under an RPL 232 term (a longer stay contemplated but not fixed) who leaves before the first October 1 owes rent to September 30 subject to mitigation; a monthly rent with nothing said about length is month to month and owes only the month begun. A constructive eviction with abandonment, or a vacate order the owner is responsible for, ends rent at the departure. An oral term longer than one year is void; the tenant is monthly from the start and may leave at the end of any month.

C7 Damage above the deposit that needs a.note: No NY extension for contractor work: the statement is due within 14 days, but it may itemize estimated costs (Toporek, App Div). The excess is a separate claim on proof (landlord's burden), and it survives a forfeiture (NY:ADJ-forfeiture-claims-survive). The balance is not a GBL consumer claim, and the limitations period is six years. Legal fees need a court order (234-a); the 234 reciprocity exposure applies. Interest on the balance runs at the lease rate until judgment where the lease sets one (capped for late rent by 238-a), otherwise at 2% for a natural-person tenant (CPLR 5004). An entity owner sues a small balance in the commercial claims part after the demand letter; a default judgment needs the 3215(g)(3) mailing. HPD registration: NYC.json. Sweep 2026-09-29: a collector of a balance that includes rent must hold a broker licence unless it is an attorney; damage-only balances need none. Utility payments under RPL 235-a are credited first. A DCWP-licensed collector that sues pleads its licence (CPLR 3015(e)).

C8 Multiple tenants, one leaving.note: One co-tenant's departure does not start the 14-day clock; it starts when the last tenant vacates. The statement goes to each co-tenant. If the deposit was one sum with no record of shares, the refund is joint and payment to one co-tenant discharges the landlord; if the landlord's records show who paid what, each co-tenant gets the remainder in proportion to what he paid (NY:ADJ-cotenants-payee). The departing co-tenant's claim before then lies against the remaining co-tenants.

C9 No forwarding address.note: Use any known email or phone number; otherwise send the statement and refund within 14 days to the vacated unit (last known address). The money stays the tenant's trust money until refunded; after 3 years unclaimed it is reported and paid to the Comptroller (ABP 1315; OSC 'Refunds Due'). Waiting for an address forfeits; whether the wait is willful is found on the whole record, and a manager is charged with knowing the rule has no missing-address exception (NY:ADJ-willful-standard). The ABP 1422 notice is excused where the only address is the vacated unit. Sweep 2026-09-29: Handoff sending the statement and refund to the last known address is not collecting rent, so it needs no broker licence, provided the statement does not demand a rent balance.

C10 Building sold mid-tenancy.note: For a stabilized unit, the buyer's liability turns on the lease date: before 2025-11-15, liability is strict whether or not the deposit was received (former 7-107(2)(a)); on or after, liability requires actual knowledge (7-107(9)). Sweep 2026-09-29: other changes on the owner side: a foreclosure receiver collects rents due and unpaid under its order; a 7-A administrator collects rent after the judgment; an individual owner's death ends the manager's authority and the estate fiduciary collects. A mortgagee with an assignment of rents collects only after it takes the rents by possession, arrangement or receiver; an owner in chapter 11 or 13 keeps collecting.

C11 Abandoned property.note: Belongings stay the tenant's until abandoned. The landlord may not hold them for rent and must allow retrieval. It may dispose of them once abandonment is shown (written notice, efforts to reach the tenant, no response for a substantial time). Moving and storage cost may be retained from the deposit. Belongings can delay the 'vacated' date.

C12 Statement due on a weekend or holida.note: Day 14 counts from the day after vacating. If it falls on a Saturday, Sunday or GCN 24 holiday, the statement and refund may be given on the next business day. Holiday calendar = Stage D input.

VA-only cases (utility withholding; dama.note: Not applicable to NY. No NY statute read provides for utility withholding or deposit-alternative insurance.

C14 Balance handed to a collector.note: Former tenant owes a balance after the deposit; it is handed to a collector. A collection agency collecting the rent part for a fee needs a New York broker licence as well as its DCWP licence; an attorney needs neither broker licence nor, for the rent part, anything under article 12-A. Damage-only balances need no broker licence. Before collecting rent, confirm who is owed it: an administrator, a receiver, HPD under a levy, a chapter 7 trustee or an estate fiduciary displaces the owner for the rent it covers. The building rent bars (certificate of occupancy, registration, rent-impairing violations) apply to multiple dwellings only. A DCWP-licensed collector that sues pleads its licence (CPLR 3015(e)). A licensed manager may pay Handoff for settlement work without fee-splitting; it may not pay an unlicensed business for leasing help. A mortgagee with an assignment of rents collects only after it takes the rents; an owner in chapter 11 or 13 keeps collecting. Registration suspends rent recovery until the owner registers, then accrued rent is recovered. A foreign LLC or corporation owner needs New York authority before suing. If S9760 becomes law, suits begun from its 90th day follow the consumer-debt pleading, notice, venue and default rules.
